title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine beyond standard thermodynamic bounds.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold, but quantum effects may challenge this. The authors explore whether indefinite causal order—a quantum feature—can alter heat flow and improve engine efficiency.
method: They consider a quantum Otto engine where two thermalization strokes occur in an indefinite causal order, modeled via a quantum switch. They analyze heat currents and work output using master equations and compare to definite order scenarios.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause anomalous heat flow (cold to hot) and increase the engine's work output and efficiency beyond the standard Otto cycle limits, even allowing operation in regimes where a definite-order engine would fail.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling heat to flow against temperature gradients and enhancing engine performance, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines.

title: Thermal Operations From Informational Equilibrium
authors: Seok Hyung Lie, Jeongrak Son, Paul Boes, Nelly H. Y. Ng, And Henrik Wilming
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie, Jeongrak Son, Paul Boes, Nelly H. Y. Ng, and Henrik Wilming

Thermal operations are quantum channels that play a central role in deriving thermodynamic limitations in quantum systems. However, they were originally defined by implementation procedures rather than by fundamental principles. Alternative models of thermal processes have been proposed, but they ob…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030403] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives thermal operations from an informational equilibrium principle, providing a foundational justification for the set of allowed operations in quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Thermal operations are central to quantum thermodynamics but were originally defined by implementation procedures rather than fundamental principles. The authors aim to derive them from a more basic informational equilibrium condition.
method: The authors introduce a principle of informational equilibrium, which states that a system and bath in thermal equilibrium should not allow net information flow. They show that this principle uniquely characterizes thermal operations as the set of quantum channels that preserve the thermal state of the joint system-bath.
result: They prove that thermal operations are exactly those channels that satisfy the informational equilibrium condition, and they demonstrate that this condition is equivalent to the standard definition of thermal operations.
conclusion: The work provides a first-principles derivation of thermal operations, strengthening the foundations of quantum thermodynamics and offering a new perspective on the set of allowed thermodynamic processes.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that grows linearly in time, with a growth rate bounded by temperature, linking quantum chaos and thermodynamics.
motivation: To quantify information gain from continuous monitoring in quantum systems and to derive a universal bound on entropy growth related to temperature.
method: Simplifies the Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring dynamical entropy for quantum systems and applies it to a monitored observable, deriving a bound using the energy-temperature uncertainty relation.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a constant times temperature, providing a quantum analog of the classical Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy and a Planckian bound.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental thermodynamic limit on the rate of information production in quantum dynamics, relevant to quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Volume-Law Protection Of Metrological Advantage
authors: Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, And Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, and Marcin Płodzień

Although entanglement can boost metrological precision beyond the standard quantum limit, the advantage often disappears with particle loss. We demonstrate that scrambling safeguards precision by dispersing information about the encoded parameter into many-body correlations. For Haar-random scrambli…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030801] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Shows that scrambling protects metrological advantage from particle loss, achieving volume-law scaling of precision.
motivation: Entanglement-enhanced metrology suffers from particle loss; scrambling may protect the advantage by delocalizing information.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of Haar-random scrambling and its effect on Fisher information under particle loss.
result: Scrambling preserves metrological advantage up to a critical loss fraction, with precision scaling as the system volume.
conclusion: Scrambling is a viable resource for robust quantum metrology, linking information scrambling to metrological utility.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: Extend the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to geometry-driven nonlinear transport, which is unexplored.
method: Derives a relation connecting dc noise to the quantum geometric tensor (curvature) using nonequilibrium Green's functions.
result: The geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation holds for nonlinear transport in quantum systems with broken time-reversal symmetry.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental link between quantum geometry and transport noise, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and nonlinear devices.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes hierarchical monogamy inequalities for the square of bipartite entanglement measures (concurrence, negativity, etc.) in N-partite systems, characterizing entanglement shareability and distribution.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks, but a unified framework for arbitrary N-partite systems was lacking.
method: The authors derive hierarchical monogamy inequalities for the square of bipartite entanglement measures, including concurrence and negativity, using algebraic properties of these measures.
result: They show that the squared concurrence and negativity satisfy a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities that tightly bound the distribution of entanglement in N-partite systems.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive characterization of entanglement shareability, with implications for quantum cryptography and multipartite quantum communication protocols.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that helps characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps for certain families of correlations.
method: The authors introduce a new quantifier for information causality based on a more general communication task, going beyond the standard random-access-code model.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the gaps, providing tighter bounds on quantum correlations.
conclusion: Information causality remains a powerful principle for delineating quantum correlations, and the proposed generalization improves its applicability.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass the classical Otto efficiency limit by consuming quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource.
motivation: To investigate whether quantum coherence can be harnessed to boost the performance of a noisy quantum heat engine beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with Markovian noise and quantify the role of coherence via resource-theoretic measures, analyzing the engine's efficiency and work output.
result: The engine exceeds the classical efficiency bound when the working medium possesses initial coherence, demonstrating coherence as a useful thermodynamic resource.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can enhance the efficiency of Markovian heat engines, providing a practical pathway to surpass classical thermodynamic limits in noisy quantum systems.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local quantum state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unlimited resources.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects.
method: They construct explicit protocols for sequential local discrimination of orthogonal bipartite states and analyze the entanglement dynamics.
result: They prove that entanglement can be preserved throughout the discrimination process, and the amount of entanglement can be unbounded.
conclusion: Sequential local discrimination can be performed without consuming entanglement, which has implications for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling resource states (entangled or private) using stabilizer channels, providing efficient protocols and bounds.
motivation: Resource states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography but are degraded by noise; distillation protocols are needed to recover high-quality states.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that can be efficiently characterized, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability, along with explicit distillation protocols.
result: They show that stabilizer channels can distill a wide range of resource states, including maximally entangled and private states, with improved rates compared to previous methods.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels offer a powerful and efficient approach to resource state distillation, with potential applications in quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that daemonic advantage can be harnessed to charge a quantum battery using a single auxiliary charger, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and standard ergotropy.
motivation: Quantum batteries are of interest for energy storage at the quantum scale, and daemonic advantage (using information to extract more work) could enhance charging. The authors aim to show that a single auxiliary can provide this advantage for multimode batteries.
method: The authors consider a quantum battery coupled to an auxiliary charger, evolve the joint system, then trace out the charger and extract energy. They define the difference between minimum daemonic ergotropy and maximum standard ergotropy as the 'daemonic gap' and show it can be bridged.
result: They find that with appropriate initial states and interactions, the daemonic gap can be closed, allowing the battery to be charged to its maximum ergotropy using only a single auxiliary.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to enhance quantum battery charging via daemonic advantage, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage devices.

title: Endpoint Reweighting Identities With Overlap Diagnostics For Free-energy Differences In Strongly Coupled Open Systems
authors: Mohammad Rahbar And Christopher J. Stein
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Rahbar and Christopher J. Stein

We develop a reweighting framework to quantify the free energy difference between two equilibrium states of a strongly coupled open system at fixed temperature. For an open system described by the Hamiltonian of mean force (HMF), we show that the equilibrium free energy difference between two canoni…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a reweighting framework using the Hamiltonian of mean force to compute free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems.
motivation: Computing free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems is challenging due to the breakdown of standard methods; a rigorous framework is needed.
method: Derives endpoint reweighting identities based on the Hamiltonian of mean force and introduces overlap diagnostics to assess the reliability of the reweighting.
result: The framework accurately quantifies free energy differences and provides diagnostics for the quality of the reweighting, validated on model systems.
conclusion: The method offers a practical and theoretically sound approach for free energy calculations in strongly coupled open systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard QKD requires fully characterized devices, while fully DI-QKD is impractical for asymmetric networks. The authors aim to bridge this gap by relaxing trust assumptions only on the more powerful node.
method: They design a protocol where one node is fully characterized and the other is untrusted, using a Bell inequality violation to certify security. Security is proven via the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves key rates comparable to device-dependent QKD while providing security against untrusted devices on one side, demonstrated in a realistic asymmetric network scenario.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance, making it suitable for asymmetric quantum networks.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillators coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare the charging power and efficiency in the quantum vs. classical limit.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) lead to a higher charging efficiency than any classical strategy, establishing a quantum advantage bound.
conclusion: Quantum batteries can outperform classical ones in efficiency, with the advantage bounded by the amount of entanglement in the system.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the more fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements has not been operationally characterized.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness certification, using quantum information-theoretic tools.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantifiable advantage in steering and randomness generation over incompatible but non-coherent measurements.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a key resource for quantum information tasks, and their operational characterization advances the understanding of quantum correlations.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing is achievable even with noisy quantum networks distributing noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision but is hindered by noise in quantum networks; this work aims to show that practical noisy networks can still yield quantum advantage.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states under realistic noise models, and analyze the impact of network imperfections.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for moderate noise levels, with the QFI scaling super-classically, and identify thresholds where classical strategies become competitive.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum-enhanced distributed sensing, providing a practical pathway for near-term quantum network applications.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging via collective effects, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption remains unclear.
method: The authors study N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum batteries under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving scaling laws for charging power and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with entanglement playing a key role, and identify dynamical scaling laws that optimize performance.
conclusion: The results provide a fundamental understanding of quantum battery charging and suggest design principles for exploiting collective quantum resources.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive.
method: Employs a cascaded quantum network architecture with a squeezed reservoir to autonomously stabilize entanglement between two remote qubits.
result: Achieves stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, robust against realistic imperfections and noise.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable and practical approach for maintaining entanglement in quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust and high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which generates steady-state entanglement through dissipative dynamics.
result: The autonomous process successfully entangles the qubits, with the reservoir providing a continuous source of quantum correlations.
conclusion: This approach offers a scalable and robust platform for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage, as the term is often used ambiguously in different contexts.
method: The authors survey and classify quantum advantage into distinct types, including computational, communication, sensing, and thermodynamic advantages, using examples from recent literature.
result: They identify a rich taxonomy of quantum advantages, showing that quantum systems can outperform classical ones in ways beyond exponential speedups, such as in precision, security, and resource efficiency.
conclusion: Understanding the diverse forms of quantum advantage is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications in quantum technologies.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity; tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and integrated single tin-vacancy centers; measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling via resonant spectroscopy and second-order correlation functions.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity (C > 1), demonstrating strong coupling between the spin and cavity mode, with Purcell enhancement and high photon indistinguishability.
conclusion: This platform is suitable for high-fidelity entanglement generation and constitutes a key building block for future quantum repeaters and distributed quantum computing.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and quantum processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in many processes thought to be classical.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a tool for generating and maintaining multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles, engineering dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to drive the system into desired entangled steady states. The cavity acts as a bus that mediates interactions and provides controlled dissipation.
result: They show that reconfigurable entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, Dicke states) can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in quantum sensing with enhanced precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for generating and exploiting multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum metrology and many-body physics.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that recording midcircuit measurement outcomes can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under measurements is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with feedback from measurement records, deriving scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that with appropriate feedback, the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size, far exceeding the polynomial scaling without feedback.
conclusion: Recording midcircuit measurements provides a practical strategy to preserve fragile quantum information, improving the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for verifying non-projective measurements, advancing quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating autonomously.
method: The authors model a quantum detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its dynamics using open quantum systems theory and deriving bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They demonstrate a trade-off between the accuracy of the measurement and the entropy produced, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic work.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental thermodynamic limits for quantum detectors, which has implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors and information-processing devices.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity enhancement reduces sensitivity to these fluctuations, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with charge noise being the main limitation that can be mitigated by cavity design and material engineering.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optically heralded entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing a transition in decoding performance based on measurement density.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in monitored quantum dynamics where measurements are used to protect encoded information.
method: The authors analyze a family of randomly monitored quantum codes, deriving conditions for successful decoding using statistical mechanics mappings and percolation theory.
result: They find a phase transition in decoding fidelity as a function of measurement rate, with optimal performance at intermediate measurement densities, and demonstrate that random measurements can improve logical error suppression.
conclusion: Random measurements can be a resource for quantum error correction, offering a new paradigm for fault-tolerant quantum computation that leverages measurement-induced phases.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance. The authors aim to design more efficient codes for near-term feasibility.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage. They analyze performance using numerical simulations.
result: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly reduce the required number of emitters and improve loss tolerance compared to symmetric tree-codes, enabling practical quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-bandgap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize the spin defect using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, including electron spin resonance and optical readout techniques.
result: They find a defect with 4-ms spin coherence time, small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO spin defects are viable for quantum information processing, particularly as qubits in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified secure QKD with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme that detects parity flips, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion technique leads to a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits with erasure conversion offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to error mitigation in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements achieving the trade-off.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces precision trade-offs due to incompatible optimal measurements, obscuring ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach to quantify the minimal trade-off and derive optimal measurements that attain it.
result: They provide a precise characterization of the trade-off and demonstrate optimal measurement strategies.
conclusion: The work advances fundamental understanding of multiparameter estimation limits and offers practical guidance for optimal measurement design.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to operational limits on reversibility.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but practical reversibility is limited by finite resolution. The authors aim to characterize this irreversibility from a thermodynamic perspective.
method: The authors analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor (e.g., detector noise) to model operational reversibility limits.
result: They show that amplification and mode mixing, combined with finite precision, lead to an irreversible entropy production, establishing a thermodynamic cost for reversing non-Hermitian dynamics.
conclusion: Precision-induced irreversibility provides a fundamental thermodynamic bound on reversibility in non-Hermitian systems, with implications for quantum control and information processing.

title: Memory Device For Photons By Exploiting Brillouin Interactions In Nanowires
authors: Hashem Zoubi
abstract:
Author(s): Hashem Zoubi

Memory devices for single photons are notable components for quantum information processing and quantum communications. The present study investigates the possibility of achieving the storage of light at the level of single photons inside nanofibers by exploiting stimulated Brillouin scattering. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013510] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a memory device for single photons using stimulated Brillouin scattering in nanofibers, enabling light storage for quantum communication.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks and repeaters; this work aims to provide a compact, on-chip solution for storing single photons.
method: The authors theoretically analyze stimulated Brillouin scattering in a nanofiber waveguide, showing that a strong pump field can create a moving grating that stores and retrieves a weak signal photon.
result: They demonstrate that storage and retrieval of single photons is feasible with high fidelity and controllable delay, using realistic parameters for silica nanowires.
conclusion: This Brillouin-based memory offers a promising approach for integrated quantum photonic circuits, directly applicable to quantum networking and communication.

title: Improving Shadow Estimation With Locally Optimal Dual Frames
authors: Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, And Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract:
Author(s): Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, and Daniel Cavalcanti

Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is a central challenge in quantum information science, yet practical implementations are fundamentally constrained by the limited number of measurement shots. In this work, we explore a variation of the classical shadows protocol in which the mea…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012428] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves classical shadow estimation by using locally optimal dual frames to reduce the number of measurement shots needed for accurate observable estimation.
motivation: Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is limited by the number of measurement shots; classical shadows offer a scalable approach but can be inefficient for certain observables.
method: The authors propose a variation of the classical shadows protocol where the measurement basis is chosen adaptively using locally optimal dual frames, optimizing the estimation variance.
result: The locally optimal dual frames reduce the required number of shots compared to standard classical shadows, especially for observables with low-rank structure.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement to shadow estimation, making it more efficient for near-term quantum devices.

title: Irreversibility Of Bound Magic States Assisted By Catalysis
authors: Yiran Wang And Yongming Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yiran Wang and Yongming Li

Quantum state transformations and resource reversibility in quantum resource theories have always been of interest to researchers. It is well known that quantum catalysts can enhance the capabilities of quantum state transformations. Previous studies have shown that bound magic states are asymptotic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012427] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the irreversibility of bound magic states in quantum resource theories and shows that catalysis can enhance reversibility.
motivation: Understanding resource reversibility is fundamental in quantum resource theories; bound magic states are known to be irreversible, but the role of catalysts in enabling reversibility is explored.
method: The authors analyze the transformation of bound magic states under free operations, introducing catalytic assistance and deriving conditions for reversibility.
result: They demonstrate that catalysis can make certain irreversible bound magic state transformations reversible, providing a complete characterization of catalytic reversibility.
conclusion: Catalysis can overcome the irreversibility of bound magic states, offering new insights into the structure of quantum resource theories and potential applications in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in simultaneously describing populations and coherences.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; the authors aim to systematically understand and quantify these limitations.
method: They formulate the problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) to find the best possible Lindblad equation that approximates a given exact dynamics, and analyze the constraints.
result: The SDP approach reveals trade-offs between accuracy in populations and coherences, providing bounds on how well Lindblad equations can capture both.
conclusion: The work offers a rigorous framework to assess the validity of Markovian approximations and guides the development of more accurate quantum master equations.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes coherent errors in a six-qubit superconducting processor with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity, using randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient algorithm implementation and error correction, but coherent errors can limit performance; understanding them is key for scalable quantum processors.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a specific connectivity graph and perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize coherent errors in single- and two-qubit gates.
result: They identify dominant coherent error sources, such as crosstalk and residual coupling, and quantify their impact on gate fidelities, showing that beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity introduces additional error channels.
conclusion: The study provides insights into error mitigation strategies for superconducting qubit networks with enhanced connectivity, guiding future hardware design and error correction protocols.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, establishing fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate the quantum bounds.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints, especially for multiple parameters. Understanding the fundamental limits and how to saturate them is crucial for practical quantum metrology.
method: The authors derive quantum Cramér-Rao bounds for multiparameter estimation in a distributed sensor network, and propose a stroboscopic measurement strategy that adaptively probes the parameters to achieve the optimal scaling.
result: They show that the stroboscopic protocol saturates the multiparameter quantum limits, achieving Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for each parameter simultaneously, and outperforms simultaneous or sequential strategies.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control provides a practical route to optimal multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, with implications for quantum-enhanced imaging, navigation, and fundamental tests.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving immunity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being insensitive to common-mode fluctuations, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable path toward quantum-enhanced sensor networks, with potential applications in precision measurements and quantum sensing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives extends qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, achieving error correction at the breakeven point where the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The passive scheme successfully extends the qubit lifetime past its physical limits, demonstrating error correction at breakeven without active measurements.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Mitigating radiation-induced correlated errors is essential for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as long-lived quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses defect centers with high-spin nuclei to repeatedly transfer entanglement from electron spins to nuclear spin qudits, accumulating multipartite entanglement.
result: Demonstrates that repeated entanglement transfer can generate high-dimensional entangled states between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical route to implementing quantum repeaters and quantum networks with enhanced dimensionality and memory lifetimes.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: Design and fabrication of an on-chip parabolic mirror with fiber in/out coupling, integrated with neutral atoms for photon collection and routing.
result: Demonstrated efficient photon extraction and coupling, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms in a compact form factor.
conclusion: The parabolic mirror on an optical chip provides a promising platform for scalable quantum network nodes, combining efficiency and mechanical stability.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitary operations required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it determines the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation, the compression rate, and the number of measurement settings in tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and has direct implications for resource theory and practical quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve state-selective, low-loss imaging and loading of atoms in an optical tweezer array, leveraging a three-level lambda system.
result: They achieve high-fidelity (>99%) nondestructive imaging and efficient loading of atom arrays, with reduced scattering and heating compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum information processing, particularly for systems requiring operation in finite magnetic fields.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilizing blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To explore exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, where long-range interactions and kinetic constraints can lead to novel phenomena beyond standard cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetically constrained long-range interactions, and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new class of non-equilibrium phases.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for studying kinetically constrained many-body physics in cavity QED, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is often impractical; variational approximations are needed.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct approximate counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The method yields higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving for several quantum control tasks.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise. The authors aim to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: They map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting code principles to cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, enabling practical suppression of spatially correlated noise in large quantum systems.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable approach to noise mitigation in quantum information processing.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function gradient under noise, connecting circuit expressivity (measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra) to noise resilience.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, and provide concentration estimates that depend on noise strength and circuit structure.
conclusion: The results offer a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational circuits and optimizing training, advancing the theory of quantum machine learning.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed.
