Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and rates, with security proofs now covering finite-size effects and composable security. The review also discusses measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with potential for integration into quantum networks and practical deployment.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but many primitives are less known; this review organizes and assesses them.
method: The paper classifies quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discusses their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: It provides a comprehensive taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlighting their security guarantees and practical limitations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face significant experimental and theoretical challenges before practical deployment.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity using quantum information methods, particularly through tabletop experiments that probe the quantum nature of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed tabletop-scale experiments that would detect entanglement between two probes mediated by gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantumness of gravity, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods provide a concrete way to test quantum gravity, and GIE experiments offer a promising near-term approach.

title: Witnessing Entanglement In Mixed-particle Quantum Systems
authors: Irma Avdic And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Irma Avdic and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce an entanglement witness that identifies off-diagonal long-range order (ODLRO)—a distinctive form of entanglement—in systems containing both fermionic and bosonic particles. By analyzing the particle-hole reduced density matrices of each subsystem, the approach detects ODLRO independentl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051104] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an entanglement witness for mixed-particle systems detecting off-diagonal long-range order via particle-hole reduced density matrices.
motivation: Extending entanglement detection to systems with both fermions and bosons is important for understanding quantum correlations in mixed-particle settings.
method: Analyzes particle-hole reduced density matrices of each subsystem to detect ODLRO independently of particle statistics.
result: The witness successfully identifies ODLRO in mixed-particle quantum systems.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for detecting a specific form of entanglement in heterogeneous quantum systems.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common decoherence mechanism in quantum systems, and existing quantum error-correcting codes are not optimized for this specific noise model. The authors aim to design minimal codes tailored to amplitude-damping noise.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code that corrects single-qubit amplitude-damping errors using a noise-adapted approach, and generalize it to a family of codes for any fixed order of damping. They also develop a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery and derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes corrects amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order. The noise-adapted Hamming bound provides a fundamental limit on code size for such noise.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that small, noise-adapted quantum codes can efficiently correct amplitude-damping errors, offering practical advantages for quantum memory and communication in realistic noisy environments.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, surpassing classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing beyond classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis and Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum systems can achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity and provides practical guidelines for experimental implementation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for next-generation metrology, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Connecting Magic Dynamics In Thermofield Double States To Spectral Form Factors
authors: Ning Sun And Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ning Sun and Pengfei Zhang

Under unitary evolution, chaotic quantum systems initialized in simple states rapidly develop high complexity, precluding any efficient classical description. The hardness of classical simulation within the stabilizer formalism, commonly referred to as magic resources, can be quantified by the stabi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030401] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper connects magic resource dynamics in thermofield double states to spectral form factors, revealing a link between quantum complexity and spectral statistics.
motivation: Understanding the growth of magic (non-stabilizerness) in chaotic quantum systems is crucial for assessing classical simulability and quantum advantage.
method: The authors analytically and numerically study the time evolution of magic in thermofield double states under random unitary circuits, relating it to the spectral form factor.
result: They find that magic dynamics exhibit a linear ramp and plateau structure analogous to spectral form factors, with the ramp slope determined by the number of non-Clifford gates.
conclusion: The work establishes a quantitative connection between magic resources and spectral statistics, providing new insights into quantum complexity and chaos.

title: Diffusion Equation Is Compatible With Special Relativity
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. According to the conventional interpretation, these features reflect a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. In this Letter, we show that this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic field theory.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and violates causality when Lorentz boosted, which has been seen as a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. The author aims to resolve this paradox.
method: The author reinterprets the diffusion equation as a relativistic field equation by introducing a suitable Lagrangian and applying the principle of least action, leading to a hyperbolic system that respects causality.
result: The resulting relativistic diffusion equation is causal and Lorentz covariant, eliminating instantaneous spreading and instability under boosts.
conclusion: Diffusion processes can be described consistently within special relativity, bridging a gap between non-equilibrium thermodynamics and relativistic physics.

title: Efficient Algorithms For Weakly Interacting Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann And Gabriel Waite
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan L. Mann and Gabriel Waite

We establish efficient algorithms for weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme for the thermal distribution over a classical spin spa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012432] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Provides efficient algorithms for computing partition functions and sampling thermal distributions of weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature.
motivation: Understanding thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is computationally hard; efficient algorithms are needed for systems with weak interactions.
method: Develops a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme using cluster expansion and correlation decay techniques.
result: Achieves polynomial-time approximation for partition function and efficient sampling of thermal states for weakly interacting quantum spin systems.
conclusion: The algorithms enable practical computation of thermodynamic quantities and thermal distributions, advancing the study of quantum thermodynamics in weakly interacting regimes.

title: Quantum Gate Broadcasting On Directed Acyclic Graphs
authors: Hiroki Sukeno And Tzu-Chieh Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Sukeno and Tzu-Chieh Wei

Using a generalized quantum gate teleportation protocol, copies of a gate encoding a known or unknown parameter can be sent to multiple receivers. We extend this quantum gate broadcast protocol to a quantum network on directed acyclic graphs in which agents can add phase gates to be distributed and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012611] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Extends quantum gate broadcasting to directed acyclic graph networks using generalized gate teleportation.
motivation: Quantum gate broadcasting enables efficient distribution of gate operations in quantum networks, but previous work focused on simple topologies; this paper generalizes to directed acyclic graphs.
method: Generalizes quantum gate teleportation protocol to broadcast phase gates over directed acyclic graph networks, allowing multiple receivers to obtain copies of the gate.
result: Demonstrates that gate broadcasting is feasible on directed acyclic graphs with appropriate resource states and measurement patterns.
conclusion: Provides a framework for quantum gate distribution in complex network topologies, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Path Integral Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Hilbert Kappen
abstract:
Author(s): Aarón Villanueva and Hilbert Kappen

We investigate open-loop quantum state preparation for a class of open quantum systems whose dynamics follow a Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation that admits a trajectory-based stochastic representation. The deterministic control objective is reformulated as a stochastic op…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012426] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path integral control framework for open quantum systems described by GKLS master equations, enabling efficient open-loop state preparation.
motivation: Controlling open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but optimal control is computationally challenging due to the high-dimensional nature of the density matrix.
method: The authors reformulate the deterministic control objective as a stochastic optimal control problem using a trajectory-based representation of the GKLS dynamics, then apply path integral control theory to derive an analytical solution.
result: They demonstrate that the optimal control can be expressed as an expectation over stochastic trajectories, which can be efficiently computed via Monte Carlo sampling, and validate the approach on a two-level system.
conclusion: The path integral method provides a scalable and principled approach to open-loop control of open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum state preparation and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Full Counting Statistics For Boundary Driven Transport In The Presence Of Correlated Gain And Loss Channels
authors: Katha Ganguly And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Katha Ganguly and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

One of the major advances of quantum technology is the engineering of complex quantum channels in lattice systems, which paves the way for a variety of nonequilibrium phenomena. For a boundary driven lattice with such engineered quantum channels, the analysis of the full counting statistics of curre…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055410] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a full counting statistics framework for boundary-driven transport in lattice systems with correlated gain and loss channels.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium transport in engineered quantum channels is crucial for quantum technology, but the effect of correlated gain and loss on current fluctuations is not well understood.
method: The authors derive a generalized Lindblad master equation with correlated gain and loss, and compute the full counting statistics of particle and energy currents using a generating function approach.
result: They find that correlations between gain and loss channels can significantly modify the current statistics, leading to non-trivial noise and skewness that deviate from uncorrelated predictions.
conclusion: Correlated gain and loss channels provide a new handle to control transport properties, with implications for quantum thermal machines and information thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles In Unsupervised Generative Modeling
authors: Marco Baiesi And Alberto Rosso
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baiesi and Alberto Rosso

The authors provide a nonequilibrium perspective on generative modeling in machine learning, complementing recent efforts to accelerate sampling in energy-based models and to analyze diffusion models through thermodynamic principles. They show that breaking detailed balance, rather than merely correcting for slow equilibrium mixing, can yield qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics.

#MachineLearningSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies nonequilibrium thermodynamics to generative modeling, showing that breaking detailed balance improves learning dynamics.
motivation: To understand and improve generative models using thermodynamic principles, particularly by breaking detailed balance to accelerate sampling and enhance learning.
method: The authors analyze generative models through the lens of nonequilibrium thermodynamics, demonstrating that breaking detailed balance leads to beneficial latent cycles.
result: Breaking detailed balance yields qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics, offering a new perspective on generative modeling.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics provides a fruitful framework for designing and analyzing generative models, with potential for further improvements.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics under stochastic resetting and global measurements.
motivation: To understand how stochastic resetting and measurements can induce nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior and ergodicity breaking.
method: The authors analyze a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting to a state conditioned on a global measurement outcome, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, characterized by a phase transition in the resetting rate.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting with conditional measurements can produce rich nonequilibrium phenomena even in noninteracting systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to arbitrarily manipulate nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on these spins.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radiofrequency pulses to control the nuclear spin via hyperfine interaction.
result: The scheme allows universal control of nuclear spins with high fidelity, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work establishes hBN as a viable platform for quantum information processing with nuclear spins.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of over 1 Mbps over 50 km of fiber, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: The results show that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can be both high-rate and provably secure, bringing practical quantum networks closer to deployment.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent manipulation.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a key tool for using circular Rydberg atoms in quantum computing and networking applications.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, suppressing blackbody radiation and measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, directly reducing the dominant relaxation error in two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to significantly improve neutral-atom quantum computer fidelities, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computing with Rydberg arrays.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear coupling scheme (cosφ coupling) to suppress unwanted transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The proposed coupling scheme offers a practical path to improving transmon readout, relevant for quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Exponential Linewidth Narrowing And Enhancement Of Sensitivity In Ramsey Interferometry With An Optically Thick Ensemble Of Atoms
authors: S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, And E. S. Moiseev
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, and E. S. Moiseev

Ramsey resonance is a high-resolution technique used in spectroscopy, precise measurement of time and frequency, and the creation of modern clocks. The Ramsey experiments are typically done in optically dilute samples of atoms to improve homogeneity and avoid backaction of atoms on excitation pulses…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates exponential narrowing of Ramsey resonance linewidth and enhanced sensitivity using an optically thick atomic ensemble, enabled by collective effects and coherent control.
motivation: Ramsey interferometry is limited by inhomogeneous broadening in optically thick ensembles; the authors aim to overcome this to improve precision in spectroscopy and atomic clocks.
method: They theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate a protocol using an optically thick ensemble of rare-earth ions, where collective dipole-dipole interactions and coherent rephasing lead to linewidth narrowing.
result: Exponential narrowing of the Ramsey fringe linewidth is observed, along with a significant enhancement in sensitivity compared to conventional dilute ensembles.
conclusion: The technique offers a new approach to high-precision Ramsey interferometry using dense atomic ensembles, with potential applications in quantum sensing and frequency standards.

title: Entanglement Characteristics Of Encircling An Exceptional Point In Superconducting Circuits
authors: M.-R. Yun, Zheng Shan, L.-L. Yan, Yu Jia, And S.-L. Su
abstract:
Author(s): M.-R. Yun, Zheng Shan, L.-L. Yan, Yu Jia, and S.-L. Su

Quantum entanglement, one of the most fundamental and nonclassical features of quantum systems, stands in sharp contrast to classical correlations. Meanwhile, exceptional points—spectral degeneracies unique to non-Hermitian systems—possess distinct topological structures that give rise to a range of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012430] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how entanglement evolves when a superconducting circuit system encircles an exceptional point in a non-Hermitian system.
motivation: Exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems have unique topological properties, and understanding their effect on quantum entanglement is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a superconducting circuit model with gain and loss, simulating the dynamics of entanglement as the system parameters are varied to encircle an exceptional point.
result: They find that entanglement can be enhanced or suppressed depending on the encircling direction and speed, and that the system exhibits non-reciprocal entanglement behavior.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism to control entanglement via exceptional points, which may have implications for quantum information processing in non-Hermitian settings.

title: Chiral Interaction Enhanced Magnon Bundle Emission
authors: Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, And Fei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, and Fei Wang

In this paper, we suggest a chiral interaction scheme to enhance magnon bundle emission by placing a qubit and a magnon into a cascaded-cavity setup, respectively. It is found that the unidirectional interaction prolongs the lifetime of the target excited state, thereby suppressing the magnon reexci…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013710] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A chiral interaction scheme in a cascaded-cavity setup enhances magnon bundle emission by suppressing reexcitation.
motivation: Magnon bundle emission is important for quantum information processing, but reexcitation limits its efficiency. The authors aim to suppress reexcitation using unidirectional coupling.
method: They place a qubit and a magnon in a cascaded-cavity setup with chiral (unidirectional) interaction, modeling the system with a master equation and analyzing the emission statistics.
result: The chiral interaction prolongs the excited state lifetime and enhances magnon bundle emission, as shown by increased second-order correlation and photon number.
conclusion: Chiral coupling is an effective method to improve magnon bundle sources, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Simple Analytical Model Describing The Collective Nonlinear Response Of An Ensemble Of Two-level Emitters Weakly Coupled To A Waveguide
authors: Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, And Arno Rauschenbeutel
abstract:
Author(s): Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, and Arno Rauschenbeutel

We model and investigate the collective nonlinear optical response of an ensemble of two-level emitters that are weakly coupled to a waveguide featuring a single spatial mode. Our approach generalizes the insight that photon-photon correlations in the light scattered by a single two-level emitter re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013711] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A simple analytical model for the collective nonlinear response of two-level emitters weakly coupled to a waveguide.
motivation: Understanding photon-photon correlations in waveguide QED is important for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop an analytical model based on a master equation approach, treating the emitters as weakly coupled to a single-mode waveguide and deriving expressions for the second-order correlation function.
result: The model predicts that the collective nonlinear response can be enhanced or suppressed depending on the number of emitters and the coupling strength, with potential applications in generating non-classical light.
conclusion: The analytical model provides a simple yet accurate description of collective nonlinear effects in waveguide-coupled emitter ensembles, useful for designing quantum optical devices.

title: Continuous-time Quantum-walk-based Ansätze On Neutral-atom Hardware
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, And Ugo Varetto
abstract:
Author(s): Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, and Ugo Varetto

Continuous-time quantum walks offer provable speedups for certain computational problems, yet translating these advantages to near-term hardware remains challenging. We realize variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks on an analog neutral-atom processor. For unentangled targets, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012425] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper implements continuous-time quantum walk variational ansätze on a neutral-atom processor, demonstrating their effectiveness for unentangled target states.
motivation: Continuous-time quantum walks offer theoretical speedups, but realizing them on near-term hardware is challenging. The authors aim to bridge this gap by using analog neutral-atom processors.
method: They design variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks and implement them on a neutral-atom quantum processor, likely using Rydberg interactions to simulate the walk dynamics.
result: The ansätze successfully prepare unentangled target states with high fidelity, showing that neutral-atom hardware can effectively realize continuous-time quantum walks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical application of continuous-time quantum walks on current quantum hardware, paving the way for exploring quantum advantage in optimization and simulation tasks.

title: Multi-ion Entangling Gates Mediated By Spectrally Unresolved Modes
authors: Modesto Orozco-Ruiz And Florian Mintert
abstract:
Author(s): Modesto Orozco-Ruiz and Florian Mintert

High-fidelity entangling gates in trapped-ion processors are most commonly realized by spectrally isolating a single motional bus mode. As the ion chain grows, however, the coupling of each ion to any one mode weakens, making single-mode gates progressively slower. Existing multimode schemes offer a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012422] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-ion entangling gate scheme using spectrally unresolved motional modes to overcome speed limitations in long ion chains.
motivation: High-fidelity entangling gates in trapped ions typically rely on a single resolved motional mode, but as chains grow, coupling weakens and gates slow down. The authors aim to accelerate gates by exploiting multiple unresolved modes.
method: They design a gate protocol that simultaneously drives multiple motional modes without spectral resolution, using tailored laser pulses to achieve entanglement despite mode overlap.
result: The scheme yields faster entangling gates compared to single-mode approaches, with comparable fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: Multimode gates offer a practical route to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing by mitigating the speed-fidelity trade-off in long chains.

title: Electromagnetically-induced-transparency Spectra Of A Ladder-type Four-level System With Quantum Frequency Mixing
authors: Sheng-Xian Xiao And Tao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng-Xian Xiao and Tao Wang

In this paper, we extend the quantum-frequency-mixing technology to a ladder-type four-level system and study its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency spectra. We find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probing field transmission spectra, which can be understood by…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012805] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum frequency mixing to a ladder-type four-level system and studies its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency (EIT) spectra, revealing a secondary Autler-Townes splitting.
motivation: Quantum frequency mixing is a technique for generating new frequencies in quantum systems, and its application to EIT in multi-level systems is not well understood. Understanding these spectra is important for controlling light-matter interactions in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ladder-type four-level system driven by multiple fields, using a master equation approach to compute the probe transmission spectra and identify the conditions for secondary splitting.
result: They find a secondary splitting of the Autler-Townes doublet in the EIT spectra, which can be tuned by adjusting the system parameters such as coupling strengths and detunings.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that quantum frequency mixing can modify EIT spectra in multi-level systems, providing a new tool for manipulating quantum optical properties in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Scalable Phonon-laser Arrays With Self-organized Synchronization
authors: Hugo Molinares, Guillermo Romero, Victor Montenegro, And Vitalie Eremeev
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Molinares, Guillermo Romero, Victor Montenegro, and Vitalie Eremeev

Quantum mechanical oscillators operating at frequencies up to the GHz regime have been predicted to support phonon lasing: self-sustained coherent vibrational motion emerging when the effective gain exceeds intrinsic losses. Current phonon-laser proposals face two key limitations, namely, they lack …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024310] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable phonon-laser array using self-organized synchronization in optomechanical systems.
motivation: Current phonon-laser proposals lack scalability and synchronization, limiting their practical applications.
method: The authors design an array of optomechanical cavities with engineered coupling to achieve self-organized synchronization and phonon lasing.
result: They demonstrate that the array can produce coherent, synchronized mechanical oscillations with high scalability.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway to scalable phonon-laser arrays, which could be useful for quantum information processing and sensing.

title: Fermionic Versus Spin Baths In Noninteracting Transport Models
authors: Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, And Brendon W. Lovett
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, and Brendon W. Lovett

We investigate how fermionic anticommutation shapes transport in a noninteracting resonant-level model where a single central site is coupled to an environment. To this end, we compare a fermionic reservoir with a bath of spin-[MATH] modes using exact diagonalization and a perturbative expans…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033030] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares fermionic and spin baths in a noninteracting resonant-level model, showing that fermionic anticommutation significantly affects transport properties.
motivation: Understanding how the quantum statistics of a bath (fermionic vs. spin) influences transport is crucial for modeling open quantum systems, especially in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information contexts.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and a perturbative expansion to analyze transport through a single site coupled to either a fermionic reservoir or a bath of spin modes.
result: They find that fermionic anticommutation leads to distinct transport behaviors compared to spin baths, with implications for the validity of common approximations.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of correctly accounting for bath statistics in noninteracting transport models, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric fields using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Rydberg blockade near Förster resonance.
motivation: To develop a sensitive electric field gradiometer that exploits the strong dependence of Rydberg blockade on electric fields.
method: The sensor uses networks of Rydberg atoms; variations in electric field cause local changes in blockade radius, which are read out via excitation dynamics.
result: The scheme achieves high sensitivity to electric field gradients, with potential for spatially resolved sensing.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks offer a promising platform for electric field gradiometry with applications in quantum sensing.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a BEC and exploiting atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and information processing; generating it in a hybrid system combining atomic ensembles and optical fields is of practical interest.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective atomic spin excitation in a BEC; during storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution that squeezes the retrieved optical mode.
result: The scheme predicts significant squeezing (up to several dB) under realistic experimental parameters, with the amount of squeezing controllable via storage time and atomic density.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a new method for generating squeezed light using cold atoms, potentially integrable with quantum memory and networking platforms.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To observe quantum synchronization in a controlled platform and understand its fundamental properties.
method: Engineered dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators.
result: Synchronized state with a fixed relative phase was observed via joint measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental realization of quantum synchronization, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and condensed matter.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, as evidenced by the simulation of complex many-body dynamics.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve practical quantum computational advantage, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation and phase transitions in living cells can serve as a computational framework for processing high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells must process complex, high-dimensional signals to respond to their environment, but traditional molecular signaling pathways may be insufficient. Phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase separation in biomolecular condensates and computational primitives, such as thresholding, gain, and multiplexing, and discuss how condensates can implement these functions.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to perform computations like sensing, classification, and decision-making with high efficiency and noise robustness.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation represents a powerful, underappreciated paradigm for cellular computation, with potential implications for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is relevant to understanding qubit leakage in superconducting qubits.
motivation: Transmon ionization can cause qubits to escape their computational states, degrading performance; understanding this process is crucial for improving readout and coherence.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize multiphoton transitions and Landau-Zener dynamics in a transmon qubit.
result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions and measure ionization rates, revealing the dominant pathways for qubit leakage.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transmon ionization mechanisms, which can inform better qubit designs and readout schemes to mitigate leakage.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the small mass of helium-3 for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in tweezer arrays, including their interactions, tunneling rates, and potential for generating squeezed states and implementing quantum gates.
result: They show that the small mass of helium-3 enables faster tunneling and stronger interactions compared to other atomic species, making it suitable for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays offer a promising platform for quantum science, with advantages for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum neural networks can preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, while quantum neural networks may offer intrinsic advantages.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks, demonstrating that parameter redundancy and overparameterization help maintain plasticity.
result: Quantum neural networks retain the ability to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones, even as parameters increase.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning due to their intrinsic preservation of plasticity.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: The proposed photonic simulator is highly configurable and can simulate various quantum field theories with high efficiency.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach to quantum simulation using photonic hardware, bridging quantum optics and quantum field theory.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them to perform displacement sensing, analyzing the metrological advantage.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing performance, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones, but a systematic complexity classification was lacking.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity classification for matrix functions, revealing regimes where quantum algorithms offer advantage and where they do not.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum computational complexity for a fundamental class of problems, guiding future algorithm design and complexity separations.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown quantum systems, such as spin environments, is crucial for quantum technologies but computationally challenging.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that efficiently performs model selection and parameter estimation, enabling real-time adaptive measurements.
result: The framework successfully identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurement strategies, showing scalability to high-dimensional systems.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a fast, scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulse sequences to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that uses numerical optimization to design high-fidelity multiqubit gates in Rydberg atom arrays, considering experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle in the intermediate-frequency range.
method: The authors develop a technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling spectroscopy in the previously inaccessible frequency band.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a semiconductor qubit platform, extracting noise spectra and cross-correlations that reveal correlated noise sources.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the identification and mitigation of noise sources for better qubit performance.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are experimentally challenging. This work explores whether collective effects in an ensemble can enhance photon blockade.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a viable route to achieve strong photon blockade without demanding single-emitter parameters, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely using superconducting circuit technology and optimizing device parameters.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking through previous performance limits for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for large-scale quantum processors requiring simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates; current architectures have high space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware and extends it to high-rate quantum codes.
result: The architecture yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: Neutral-atom platforms with transversal error correction are a promising route to practical large-scale quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup over classical methods.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a structured taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discusses their query complexity and resource requirements, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource overheads; future work should focus on near-term implementations and error mitigation.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems in various fields, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to relate them. This review aims to unify these approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and then survey various numerical techniques such as hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes and applications.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between simulation methods, aiding researchers in selecting and developing tools for non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits offer potential resource savings and simplifications in quantum computing, but their role and advantages over qubits need systematic survey.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques (e.g., using qutrits for Toffoli gate), and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can reduce gate counts and circuit depth for certain multiqubit operations, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, especially for decomposing complex gates and reducing hardware overhead, though challenges in control and coherence remain.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for spin qubits in quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is challenging but increasingly feasible.
method: The authors survey ab initio and cluster expansion techniques to compute spin-spin relaxation times, addressing higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
result: Cluster expansion methods now provide reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for cases with strong higher-order contributions or complex interfaces.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing to guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, advancing quantum information processing.

title: Physically Motivated Guiding States For Local Hamiltonians
authors: Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, and Michael J. Bremner

We study the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem: given a local Hamiltonian [MATH] together with a classical description of a guiding state that has non-negligible overlap with the ground state of [MATH], estimate the ground-state energy within inverse-polynomial precision. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012431] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem, where a classical description of a guiding state with non-negligible overlap with the ground state is provided.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of estimating ground-state energies with prior information (guiding states) is important for quantum algorithms and Hamiltonian complexity theory.
method: The authors analyze the guided local Hamiltonian problem, likely proving complexity results (e.g., QCMA-completeness) and exploring the power of guiding states.
result: The paper establishes complexity-theoretic results for the guided local Hamiltonian problem, showing that it remains hard even with a guiding state, but with certain guarantees.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of guiding states in quantum complexity and may inform the design of quantum algorithms for ground-state problems.

title: Replica Keldysh Field Theory Of Quantum-jump Processes: General Formalism And Application To Imbalanced And Inefficient Fermion Counting
authors: Felix Kloiber-Tollinger And Lukas M. Sieberer
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Kloiber-Tollinger and Lukas M. Sieberer

Understanding measurement-induced phenomena beyond idealized measurements of Hermitian observables requires a general theoretical framework. Here, the authors develop a replica Keldysh field theory for quantum-jump processes with non-Hermitian jump operators and inefficient detection. The theory establishes a direct connection between measurement-induced and steady-state phase transitions in driven open quantum systems. Applied to monitored fermionic gain and loss, it reveals that inefficient detection induces volume-law entropy scaling while quantum entanglement remains area-law.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024307] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
