tldr: Develops a replica Keldysh field theory for quantum-jump processes with non-Hermitian jump operators and inefficient detection, revealing distinct scaling of entropy and entanglement.
motivation: Understanding measurement-induced phenomena beyond idealized measurements requires a general theoretical framework for quantum-jump processes with non-Hermitian operators and inefficient detection.
method: The authors develop a replica Keldysh field theory that establishes a direct connection between measurement-induced and steady-state phase transitions in driven open quantum systems.
result: Applied to monitored fermionic gain and loss, the theory reveals that inefficient detection induces volume-law entropy scaling while quantum entanglement remains area-law.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to analyze measurement-induced phase transitions in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithm protocol that allows a client to outsource VQA computations to an untrusted quantum server while ensuring correctness.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum devices, but small-scale users lack access to quantum hardware. Delegating computation to a quantum cloud raises trust issues, so a verification mechanism is needed.
method: The protocol uses trap qubits and measurement-based verification techniques to detect malicious behavior by the server, building on existing blind quantum computing and verification frameworks.
result: The protocol achieves end-to-end verifiability for VQAs with polynomial overhead, and the authors prove security against a dishonest server under standard assumptions.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated VQAs are feasible and can enable secure quantum cloud services, bridging the gap between near-term quantum hardware and practical applications.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, leveraging initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating quantum circuits classically is often intractable, but for small patches of the expectation landscape, classical surrogates may be efficient and useful for optimization or understanding.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape using initial data from quantum computers, likely involving machine learning or regression techniques.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values in the targeted subregion with reduced quantum resources.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical hybrid quantum-classical strategy for exploring quantum landscapes, potentially aiding in variational algorithms or quantum circuit design.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice to represent ancillary degrees of freedom, combined with moment-matching techniques to approximate the nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing and algorithm design.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems, demonstrating extrapolation beyond training data.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and predict long-time behavior.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators, which learn mappings in frequency space, to approximate the Floquet Hamiltonian and time evolution of observables from limited trajectory data.
result: The method accurately reproduces Floquet Hamiltonians and observable dynamics, and extrapolates to longer times and different driving parameters not seen during training.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a powerful tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Randomly Measured Quantum Particles And Thermal Noise
authors: Victor Gurarie
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Gurarie

We consider the motion of a quantum particle whose position is measured in random places at random moments in time. We contrast this motion with the motion of a quantum particle in a potential which varies randomly in space and in time, which could also be thought of as (possibly thermal) noise. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012205] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the motion of a quantum particle under random position measurements and compares it to motion in a random potential, linking to thermal noise.
motivation: To understand the effect of random measurements on quantum dynamics and contrast it with classical thermal noise.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a quantum particle subjected to random position measurements at random times, modeled as a stochastic process.
result: The random measurement process leads to diffusive behavior similar to classical Brownian motion, with a diffusion constant related to measurement rate.
conclusion: Random measurements can mimic thermal noise, providing a quantum analog of classical stochastic dynamics.

title: Weakly Fault-tolerant Computation In A Quantum Error-detecting Code
authors: Christopher Gerhard And Todd A. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Gerhard and Todd A. Brun

Many current quantum error-correcting codes that achieve full fault tolerance suffer from having low ratios of logical to physical qubits and significant overhead. This makes them difficult to implement on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers and results in the inability to perform qua…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012429] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a weakly fault-tolerant computation scheme within a quantum error-detecting code, reducing overhead compared to fully fault-tolerant codes.
motivation: Fully fault-tolerant quantum error-correcting codes require high overhead, making them impractical for near-term quantum devices. The authors aim to develop a more resource-efficient approach that still provides some protection against errors.
method: The authors design a computation protocol using a quantum error-detecting code that detects errors but does not correct them, combined with a method to continue computation upon error detection, achieving weak fault tolerance.
result: They demonstrate that the scheme can tolerate a certain level of noise with lower qubit overhead than fully fault-tolerant codes, though it does not guarantee arbitrary-length computations.
conclusion: Weakly fault-tolerant computation in error-detecting codes offers a practical intermediate step for near-term quantum devices, balancing error protection and resource requirements.

title: Entanglement-entropy-based Scaling Relation In Qaoa Tensor Network Simulations For The Maxcut Problem
authors: Goro Miki And Yasuhiro Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Goro Miki and Yasuhiro Tokura

With the rapid development of quantum computers in recent years, the importance of performance evaluation in quantum algorithms has been increasing. One method that has gained attention for performing this evaluation on classical computers is tensor networks. Tensor networks not only reduce the comp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012610] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses tensor network simulations to study entanglement entropy scaling in QAOA for MaxCut, proposing a scaling relation to predict algorithm performance.
motivation: Evaluating quantum algorithms on classical computers is important; tensor networks offer a way to simulate QAOA, but understanding entanglement growth is key to scalability.
method: The authors perform tensor network simulations of QAOA for MaxCut on random graphs, measuring entanglement entropy and fitting a scaling relation.
result: They find a scaling relation between entanglement entropy and problem size, which can be used to estimate the computational cost of tensor network simulations.
conclusion: The scaling relation provides a practical tool for predicting when tensor network simulations of QAOA become intractable, guiding algorithm design.

title: Entanglement Dynamics In Minimal Kitaev Chains
authors: Vimalesh Kumar Vimal And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Vimalesh Kumar Vimal and Jorge Cayao

Minimal Kitaev chains host Majorana quasiparticles, which, although not topologically protected, exhibit spatial nonlocality and hence are expected to be useful for quantum information tasks. In this work, we consider two- and three-site Kitaev chains and investigate the dynamics of bipartite and mu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034308] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in minimal Kitaev chains with two and three sites, focusing on Majorana quasiparticles and their nonlocality.
motivation: Minimal Kitaev chains host Majorana quasiparticles with spatial nonlocality, which are expected to be useful for quantum information tasks, but their entanglement dynamics have not been fully explored.
method: The authors consider two- and three-site Kitaev chains and numerically investigate the dynamics of bipartite and multipartite entanglement using measures like concurrence and negativity.
result: They find that entanglement dynamics depend on the chain length and initial conditions, with Majorana nonlocality leading to distinct entanglement patterns.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the role of Majorana quasiparticles in quantum information processing, though the systems are minimal and lack topological protection.

title: Control Protocols For Harmonically Confined Run-and-tumble Particles
authors: Marco Baldovin And Alessandro Manacorda
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baldovin and Alessandro Manacorda

A run-and-tumble particle is placed in a harmonic confining potential, and an external agent can vary the tumbling rate and the strength of the trap over time. The objective is to find time-dependent control protocols steering the system between assigned end states, in a prescribed time interval. Under suitable assumptions, the authors find analytical solutions that are tested against simulations and provide insightful intuition.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014112] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives optimal control protocols for a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic trap, minimizing work or maximizing efficiency.
motivation: Understanding how to control active matter systems is important for applications in microrobotics and biological physics, but the paper focuses on a specific model without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analytically solve for time-dependent tumbling rate and trap strength that steer the system between states, using optimal control theory and assuming a linear response regime.
result: They find explicit protocols that minimize work or achieve target states, validated by simulations.
conclusion: The work provides insight into control of active particles but is too applied and narrow for the user's research focus on quantum information thermodynamics.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:
Author(s): Ievgen I. Arkhipov

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033037] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, addressing the ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the lack of Hermitian conjugation between left and right eigenvectors.
method: The author introduces a covariant approach to define the Berry connection and curvature that is independent of the choice of biorthogonal basis, using a gauge-invariant formalism.
result: The covariant Berry connection is shown to reduce to the standard Hermitian result in the Hermitian limit and captures topological invariants such as the Chern number in non-Hermitian systems.
conclusion: The work provides a consistent geometric framework for non-Hermitian systems, which is important for understanding topological phases in open quantum systems.

title: Sequential Analysis In A Continuous Spin-noise Quantum Sensor
authors: E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, And J. Calsamiglia
abstract:
Author(s): E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, and J. Calsamiglia

Many control and detection applications require real-time analysis of signals from sensors, in order to quickly and accurately act upon events revealed by the sensors. Such signal analysis benefits from statistical models of signal and sensor behavior. This creates a need for data analysis methods t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033038] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a sequential analysis method for continuous spin-noise quantum sensors, enabling real-time detection of magnetic field changes.
motivation: Real-time analysis of sensor signals is needed for control and detection applications, but existing methods are often offline or require large datasets.
method: The authors propose a sequential hypothesis testing framework based on the Fisher information and Cramér-Rao bound, applied to a spin-noise magnetometer model.
result: The method achieves faster detection of field changes compared to batch processing, with controlled false alarm rates.
conclusion: Sequential analysis is effective for continuous quantum sensors, improving response time without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to gradually increase the expressivity of quantum machine learning models during training to improve optimization and generalization.
motivation: Training quantum machine learning models is challenging due to the difficulty of establishing effective inductive biases and avoiding barren plateaus.
method: The authors introduce a training scheme that starts with a restricted model and progressively adds complexity by increasing the number of layers or parameters, using a curriculum learning approach.
result: The gradual complexity method improves training convergence and test performance compared to standard training on several benchmark tasks.
conclusion: Gradually increasing model complexity is a promising strategy for training quantum machine learning models, potentially mitigating issues like barren plateaus.

title: Learning Minimal Representations Of Fermionic Ground States
authors: Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, And Stefano Polla
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, and Stefano Polla

We introduce an unsupervised machine-learning framework that discovers optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states. Using an autoencoder neural network architecture on reduced density matrix data from [MATH]-site Fermi-Hubbard models, we identify minimal latent spaces with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033014] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised machine learning framework using autoencoders to find minimal latent representations of fermionic ground states from reduced density matrix data.
motivation: To discover compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states that capture essential physical features, potentially aiding in understanding and simulation.
method: Applied an autoencoder neural network to reduced density matrix data from Fermi-Hubbard models, identifying minimal latent spaces with a specific number of degrees of freedom.
result: The framework successfully identified minimal latent representations, demonstrating that ground states can be compressed to a low-dimensional latent space.
conclusion: The approach provides a data-driven method to extract minimal representations of quantum states, which may be useful for quantum information tasks but is primarily a machine learning application.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing optical quantum state generation, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Generating non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods suffer from low success rates. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: They define control parameters beyond the stellar rank, enabling a structured approach to design and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems.
result: The proposed parameters allow orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success probability of generating essential non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a scalable path for producing non-Gaussian states, which is important for quantum computing and communication applications.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is important for quantum supremacy experiments and random circuit sampling, but the paper's focus is on statistical properties rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic bounds.
method: The authors analyze random quantum circuits with noise using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to derive universal anticoncentration properties.
result: They find that anticoncentration is universal across different circuit architectures and exhibits distinct regimes depending on circuit depth relative to noise strength.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for anticoncentration in noisy circuits, but the connection to information thermodynamics is indirect, as the paper does not address thermodynamic costs or information processing bounds.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods struggle with large multiqubit unitaries. The authors aim to extend the reach of stabilizer-based simulation by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for larger systems, building on the Gottesman-Knill theorem and Clifford circuit properties.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits with significantly more qubits than previous methods, achieving practical speedups.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the verification of quantum devices and the study of quantum advantage.

title: Quantum-Error-Correction-Inspired Noise Mitigation For Wavelike Dark Matter Searches With Quantum Sensors
authors: Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, And Thanaporn Sichanugrist
abstract:
Author(s): Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, and Thanaporn Sichanugrist

We propose a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol for enhancing the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors. Our protocol uses multiple sensors to mitigate the noise affecting each sensor individually, allowing for the suppression of excitation noise …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol to improve sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches using quantum sensors.
motivation: Dark matter searches with quantum sensors are limited by noise; a protocol to suppress excitation noise can enhance detection sensitivity.
method: Uses multiple quantum sensors and a noise mitigation protocol inspired by quantum error correction to reduce individual sensor noise.
result: The protocol suppresses excitation noise, improving the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction techniques can be adapted for noise mitigation in quantum sensing applications beyond computing.

title: Nonequilibrium Orders In Parametrically Driven Field Theories
authors: Carl Philipp Zelle, Romain Daviet, Andrew J. Millis, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Carl Philipp Zelle, Romain Daviet, Andrew J. Millis, and Sebastian Diehl

Driving quantum materials with coherent light has proven a powerful platform to realize a plethora of interesting phases and transitions, ranging from ferroelectricity to superconductivity and limit cycles in pumped magnonics. In this paper we develop the field theoretical framework to describe none…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024308] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Develops a field-theoretic framework for nonequilibrium orders in parametrically driven systems, focusing on limit cycles and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand and classify nonequilibrium phases induced by coherent driving, such as ferroelectricity and superconductivity, using a unified field theory.
method: Constructs a Keldysh field theory for parametrically driven bosonic systems, analyzing the effective action and renormalization group flow.
result: Identifies conditions for limit-cycle phases and nonequilibrium phase transitions, characterized by spontaneous time-translation symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to describe driven-dissipative phases and may guide experimental searches for nonequilibrium orders.

title: Limits Of Clifford Disentangling In Tensor Network States
authors: Sergi Masot-Llima, Piotr Sierant, Paolo Stornati, And Artur Garcia-Saez
abstract:
Author(s): Sergi Masot-Llima, Piotr Sierant, Paolo Stornati, and Artur Garcia-Saez

Tensor network methods leverage the limited entanglement of quantum states to efficiently simulate many-body systems. Alternatively, Clifford circuits provide a framework for handling highly entangled stabilizer states, which have low magic and are thus also classically tractable. Clifford tensor ne…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024311] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the limits of using Clifford circuits to disentangle tensor network states, showing that while Clifford disentangling can reduce entanglement, it cannot achieve a product state for generic states.
motivation: Tensor network methods are limited by entanglement, while Clifford circuits can handle highly entangled stabilizer states. The goal is to combine these approaches to improve simulation of many-body systems.
method: The authors define Clifford disentangling as applying a Clifford circuit to reduce entanglement in a tensor network state, and analyze its effectiveness using measures like stabilizer Rényi entropy and magic.
result: They find that Clifford disentangling can reduce entanglement but not eliminate it entirely; the residual entanglement is related to the non-stabilizerness (magic) of the state.
conclusion: Clifford disentangling is a useful tool but has fundamental limits; for generic states, the remaining entanglement after optimal Clifford disentangling is lower bounded by the magic of the state.

title: Emergence Of Darcy's Law And Apparent Violation Of Onsager Symmetry In Multiphase Transport
authors: Omid Tavakkoli, Dick Bedeaux, Signe Kjelstrup, Steffen Berg, Marcel Moura, Ying Da Wang, Peyman Mostaghimi, And Ryan T. Armstrong
abstract:
Author(s): Omid Tavakkoli, Dick Bedeaux, Signe Kjelstrup, Steffen Berg, Marcel Moura, Ying Da Wang, Peyman Mostaghimi, and Ryan T. Armstrong

We introduce a nonequilibrium thermodynamic (NET) framework for immiscible two-phase flow in porous media, in which the total flux of both phases is driven by the gradient of an effective pressure. We show that the classical two-phase Darcy formulation emerges as a projected limit of the full linear…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015103] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonequilibrium thermodynamic framework for two-phase flow in porous media, showing that Darcy's law emerges from a linear force-flux relation and that Onsager symmetry appears violated due to coarse-graining.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic basis of multiphase transport in porous media and resolve apparent violations of Onsager symmetry observed in experiments.
method: The authors apply nonequilibrium thermodynamics (NET) to derive a linear force-flux relation for immiscible two-phase flow, then project it to obtain the classical Darcy formulation, and analyze the role of coarse-graining in the apparent Onsager symmetry breaking.
result: Darcy's law is recovered as a projected limit of the full linear NET description, and the apparent violation of Onsager symmetry is explained by the elimination of cross-coupling terms during coarse-graining.
conclusion: The NET framework provides a consistent thermodynamic foundation for multiphase flow, reconciling empirical observations with fundamental thermodynamic principles.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging because logical gates often require braiding or complex operations; this work aims to simplify the process.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding.
result: They demonstrate that universal fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in 2D without braiding, using non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation in two-dimensional architectures.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically incurs large overhead in qubits and time; this work aims to reduce both by leveraging good quantum LDPC codes.
method: The authors design a protocol that combines parallelized code surgery with locally testable state preparation, exploiting the properties of good quantum LDPC codes.
result: They demonstrate constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more practical.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery, optimized for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to conventional magic state distillation methods, making it more practical for near-term quantum computers.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path to reduce the resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian spectral topology in a cold Rydberg gas, demonstrating interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a rich phenomenon in open systems, but experimental realizations in many-body quantum systems are scarce. Cold Rydberg gases offer a tunable dissipative platform to explore such topology.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform and map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocity that depend on the scan direction, confirming non-Hermitian topological features.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cold Rydberg gases are a viable platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, opening avenues for exploring topological phases in open quantum systems.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel, pruning unlikely ones to balance accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical resources.
conclusion: Beam search decoding is a practical solution for quantum LDPC codes, enabling real-time error correction with high fidelity.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient implementations of non-Clifford gates on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that enable fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, using a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: A family of scalable circuits is presented, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder on planar chips.
conclusion: The proposed circuits provide a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to assess the protection and feasibility of Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality using numerical simulations.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish topological Majorana modes from trivial Andreev bound states, and evaluate their suitability for braiding operations.
conclusion: The work offers practical guidelines for identifying truly non-Abelian Majorana bound states in experiments, but the focus is on platform characterization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Sound Of Electrons Shattering: Current Noise Composition Laws For Electron Fractionalization
authors: Adarsh S. Patri, Josephine J. Yu, Yi-Ming Wu, T. Senthil, And Hart Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Adarsh S. Patri, Josephine J. Yu, Yi-Ming Wu, T. Senthil, and Hart Goldman

We develop a theory of the nonequilibrium current response for metallic systems near quantum critical points where electronic quasiparticles fractionalize, such as systems near continuous metal-insulator transitions or composite Fermi liquid to Fermi liquid transitions. Applying a generalized respon…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055117] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of nonequilibrium current noise near quantum critical points where electrons fractionalize.
motivation: To understand the signatures of electron fractionalization in transport noise, which is a fundamental aspect of strongly correlated systems.
method: Uses a generalized response theory to compute current noise and derive composition laws for fractionalized excitations.
result: Derives composition laws for current noise that reveal the fractionalized nature of the charge carriers.
conclusion: Current noise measurements can serve as a probe of electron fractionalization in metallic systems near quantum critical points.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to exploit commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting T gates through Pauli-based circuits, thereby reducing the overall T-count.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The work provides a new technique for T-count reduction, which is important for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlation dynamics and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which can lead to novel optical responses and quantum metastable phases.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways using strong static or periodic fields, and mechanisms governing photodoped carrier evolution.
result: Highlights key mechanisms for emergent metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, revealing rich nonequilibrium phenomena and potential for new functionalities.

title: Toric Code Under Antiferromagnetic Isotropic Heisenberg Interactions
authors: Won Jang, Robert Peters, And Thore Posske
abstract:
Author(s): Won Jang, Robert Peters, and Thore Posske

We investigate the impact of an isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, focusing on the resulting quantum phase transition and the nature of the phase that emerges beyond topological order. Using neural-network quantum states, we compute ground states over a wide range…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033008] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of an antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, revealing a quantum phase transition from topological order to a trivial paramagnet.
motivation: Understanding the stability of topological order under perturbations is crucial for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states (NQS) to compute ground states of the perturbed toric code Hamiltonian for various perturbation strengths.
result: They find a continuous quantum phase transition from the topological phase to a trivial paramagnetic phase at a finite critical perturbation strength.
conclusion: The toric code's topological order is robust up to a finite perturbation, beyond which it gives way to a trivial phase, demonstrating the utility of NQS for studying frustrated quantum magnets.

title: Imaginary Time Formalism For Causal Nonlinear Response Functions
authors: Sounak Sinha And Barry Bradlyn
abstract:
Author(s): Sounak Sinha and Barry Bradlyn

It is well established that causal linear response functions can be found by computing the much simpler imaginary-time-ordered Matsubara functions and performing an analytic continuation. This principle is the basis for much of our understanding of linear response for interacting and disordered syst…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045113] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the imaginary-time formalism to nonlinear response functions, providing a method to compute causal nonlinear response via analytic continuation of Matsubara-like functions.
motivation: Linear response theory is well understood via imaginary-time formalism, but nonlinear response lacks a similar framework. The authors aim to fill this gap for interacting and disordered systems.
method: They develop a diagrammatic approach for nonlinear response functions in the imaginary-time domain, analogous to the Matsubara technique for linear response, and establish analytic continuation rules to obtain real-time causal functions.
result: They derive explicit formulas for second- and third-order nonlinear response functions in terms of imaginary-time-ordered correlation functions, and demonstrate the method on simple models.
conclusion: The imaginary-time formalism can be systematically extended to nonlinear response, enabling efficient computation of higher-order response in quantum many-body systems.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:
Author(s): Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, and Yoshinobu Kawahara

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033032] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution, improving accuracy and efficiency for ground state calculations.
motivation: Neural quantum states are powerful but often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated architecture that improves performance and interpretability.
method: The authors introduce a framework where the neural network ansatz is derived from a latent imaginary-time evolution, using a transformer architecture to capture long-range correlations and employing a variational Monte Carlo approach for optimization.
result: The proposed method achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence compared to standard neural quantum states on benchmark spin models, including the Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising models.
conclusion: The physics-inspired design of neural quantum states via latent imaginary-time evolution offers a principled way to construct efficient and accurate variational ansätze for quantum many-body systems.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a tensor network contraction algorithm with exponential convergence, improving upon belief propagation.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard, and belief propagation often fails for loopy graphs; systematic corrections are needed.
method: The authors introduce cluster corrections to belief propagation, enabling polynomial-time contraction with rigorous error bounds.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence in approximation error, outperforming standard belief propagation on various tensor networks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected belief propagation provides a practical and provably accurate method for tensor network contraction.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: The algorithm achieves a provable exponential speedup over classical methods for certain inputs.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential quantum advantage for a practical problem, but the relevance to quantum information theory is limited.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup. The authors aim to provide a complete pipeline from state preparation to measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
method: The algorithm uses a Hadamard test with controlled unitary operations derived from braid group representations, implemented on a Quantinuum H2 trapped-ion device with up to 36 qubits and 108 two-qubit gates.
result: The experimental results show agreement with exact values for small knots, but the algorithm's depth and fidelity limitations prevent scaling to classically intractable instances.
conclusion: While the work demonstrates a proof-of-principle, the current hardware constraints mean it does not yet achieve quantum advantage or provide new information-theoretic insights.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and the state version extends it to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry learning.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is crucial for perception and cognition; statistical physics offers tools to bridge theory and experiment.
method: The authors review maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural data, demonstrating predictive power akin to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative framework for analyzing neural network dynamics, but the paper is primarily a review of biological applications.

title: Demonstration Of Deuterium’s Enhanced Sensitivity To Symmetry Violations Governed By The Standard-Model Extension
authors: A. Nanda, D. Comparat, O. Dulieu, S. Lahs, C. Malbrunot, L. Nowak, M. C. Simon, And E. Widmann
abstract:
Author(s): A. Nanda, D. Comparat, O. Dulieu, S. Lahs, C. Malbrunot, L. Nowak, M. C. Simon, and E. Widmann

We have performed hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium and searched for violations of [MATH] and Lorentz symmetry that would manifest as sidereal variations of the observed transition frequencies. Several nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model extensi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031802] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests Lorentz and CPT symmetry violations in deuterium using hyperfine spectroscopy, but does not align with the specified research directions.
motivation: To search for violations of Lorentz and CPT symmetry in deuterium, which could indicate new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium, searching for sidereal variations in transition frequencies.
result: Constraints on nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension were obtained, but no significant violations were found.
conclusion: The experiment sets improved limits on certain symmetry-violating coefficients, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Commensurate-Incommensurate Mott Transition Without Magnetic Field: Emergence Of Nematic Luttinger Liquid In Xxz Chain
authors: Julien Fitouchi And Natalia Chepiga
abstract:
Author(s): Julien Fitouchi and Natalia Chepiga

We investigate the zero magnetization and ground state phase diagram of a spin-[MATH] chain with competing ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor and antiferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbor exchange couplings in the strongly interacting regime. Using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations, w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036503] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the zero-magnetization ground state phase diagram of a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, revealing a nematic Luttinger liquid phase.
motivation: To understand the emergence of nematic order and commensurate-incommensurate transitions in quantum spin chains without an external magnetic field.
method: Density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations are used to compute the ground state phase diagram.
result: A nematic Luttinger liquid phase is found, and the commensurate-incommensurate Mott transition is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides insights into exotic quantum phases in one-dimensional systems with competing interactions.

title: Pseudochiral Phonons From Octupolar Magnetic Order
authors: Ruairidh Sutcliffe, Kathleen Hart, Swati Chaudhary, And Arun Paramekanti
abstract:

Motivated by the recent discovery of anomalously large magnetic response of chiral phonons in dipolar magnets, we introduce the concept of pseudochiral phonons which are shown to emerge in multipolar magnets. We consider Raman active quantum phonons, such as doublet [MATH] phonons $({d}_{{x}^{2}−…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036703] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces pseudochiral phonons arising from octupolar magnetic order, focusing on a condensed matter phenomenon without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Recent discovery of large magnetic response of chiral phonons in dipolar magnets motivates exploring similar effects in multipolar magnets.
method: The authors theoretically analyze Raman active quantum phonons in multipolar magnets, introducing the concept of pseudochiral phonons.
result: They show that pseudochiral phonons emerge from octupolar magnetic order, exhibiting distinct properties from conventional chiral phonons.
conclusion: This work expands the understanding of phonon-magnetism coupling but does not address quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

authors: Pier Francesco Monni, Gherardo Vita, Zhen Xu, And Hua Xing Zhu

We investigate the charge-charge correlation (QQC) in electron-positron annihilation as a probe of charge dynamics in quantum chromodynamics. While generally divergent beyond leading order, we show that the QQC is infrared and collinear safe in the back-to-back limit, a property that we dub leading-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031901] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge-charge correlation in QCD, a topic in high-energy particle physics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand charge dynamics in quantum chromodynamics via electron-positron annihilation.
method: Theoretical analysis of charge-charge correlation in the back-to-back limit, showing infrared and collinear safety.
result: The charge-charge correlation is infrared and collinear safe in the back-to-back limit, a property dubbed leading-…
conclusion: The back-to-back limit provides a safe observable for studying charge dynamics in QCD.

title: Symmetric Localization Of ${ν}_{tot}=4/3$ Fractional Topological Insulator Edges
authors: Yang-Zhi Chou And Sankar Das Sarma
abstract:
Author(s): Yang-Zhi Chou and Sankar Das Sarma

Motivated by the recent twisted [MATH] experiment [Wang et al., Magnetic Signatures of a Putative Fractional Topological insulator in twisted [MATH],
tldr: This paper develops a disordered interacting edge theory for a fractional topological insulator at ν=4/3, focusing on edge localization and transport signatures.
motivation: Recent experiments on twisted MoTe2 suggest a fractional topological insulator, but the edge physics and disorder effects are not well understood.
method: The authors construct a one-dimensional edge theory incorporating disorder and interactions, and analyze the localization properties using renormalization group and bosonization techniques.
result: They find that the edge states can be localized by disorder, leading to a suppression of transport, and identify signatures of the fractional topological insulator phase.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding edge physics in fractional topological insulators and offers predictions for future experiments.

title: Stimulated Magnonic Frequency Combs
authors: Xueyu Guo, Tianci Gong, Guibin Lan, Mengying Guo, Xiufeng Han, Guoqiang Yu, Peng Yan, And Qi Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xueyu Guo, Tianci Gong, Guibin Lan, Mengying Guo, Xiufeng Han, Guoqiang Yu, Peng Yan, and Qi Wang

Magnonic frequency combs, characterized by a series of discrete frequency lines, have emerged as a promising frontier in magnon spintronics, with potential applications in advanced information processing and sensing technologies. Although the three-magnon scattering process is widely recognized as a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036701] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of stimulated magnonic frequency combs in a magnon spintronics system.
motivation: Magnonic frequency combs have potential applications in information processing and sensing, but their generation via stimulated processes has not been demonstrated.
method: The authors use a three-magnon scattering process in a magnetic thin film to generate frequency combs, driven by a microwave field.
result: They observe discrete frequency lines characteristic of frequency combs, with tunable spacing and power dependence.
conclusion: Stimulated magnonic frequency combs are realized, opening new possibilities for magnon-based signal processing.

title: Signatures Of Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$
authors: Sajid Husain, Maya Ramesh, Qian Song, Sergei Prokhorenko, Shashank Kumar Ojha, Surya Narayan Panda, Xinyan Li, Yousra Nahas, Yogesh Kumar, Pushpendra Gupta, Tenzin Chang, Alan Ji-In Jung, Rogério de Sousa, James G. Magnons provide a route to ultrafast transport and nondestructive readout of spin-based information transfer. Here, we report magnon transport and its emergent anisotropic nature in [MATH] layers confined between ultrathin layers of the antiferromagnet [MATH]. Because…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036702] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magnon transport and its anisotropic nature in BiFeO3, focusing on altermagnetism signatures.
motivation: To explore magnon transport in antiferromagnetic BiFeO3 and its potential for spin-based information transfer.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis of magnon transport in BiFeO3 layers confined between antiferromagnetic layers.
result: Observation of anisotropic magnon transport, indicating altermagnetic behavior.
conclusion: BiFeO3 exhibits altermagnetic signatures, which could be relevant for spintronics.

title: Pushy Random Walk: A Minimal Model For Transport In Deformable Media
authors: Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Itamar Shitrit, Shlomi Reuveni, And Sidney Redner
abstract:
Author(s): Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Itamar Shitrit, Shlomi Reuveni, and Sidney Redner

In a minimal model of a pushy random walk, a moving tracer can displace obstacles, giving rise to new diffusive behaviors in both 1D and 2D.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037101] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model of a pushy random walk where a tracer displaces obstacles, leading to new diffusive behaviors in 1D and 2D.
motivation: To understand transport in deformable media where obstacles can be moved by a tracer, which is common in biological and soft matter systems.
method: Analytical and numerical study of a random walk model where the tracer pushes obstacles aside, modifying the environment.
result: The pushy random walk exhibits anomalous diffusion and non-Gaussian displacement distributions in both one and two dimensions.
conclusion: The model captures essential features of transport in deformable media and predicts novel diffusive regimes.

title: Direct Observation Of Energy Transport Dynamics And High Thermal Conductance Across Single Solid-Molecule Junctions
authors: Md. Shahriar Hossain Shuvo, Xing He, Mithun Ghosh, And Ding-Shyue Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Md. Shahriar Hossain Shuvo, Xing He, Mithun Ghosh, and Ding-Shyue Yang

We report dynamic energy transport across multicomponent molecular junctions observed at the atomic level. A clear temporal sequence of energy transfer is revealed at early times following photoexcitation of Au(111) bonded with self-assembled monolayers of alkanethiols: from the gold surface layer t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 038001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports direct observation of energy transport dynamics and high thermal conductance across single solid-molecule junctions using ultrafast electron diffraction.
motivation: Understanding energy transport at the atomic level in molecular junctions is crucial for nanoscale thermal management and molecular electronics.
method: The authors use femtosecond electron diffraction to probe the temporal sequence of energy transfer after photoexcitation of Au(111) with self-assembled alkanethiol monolayers.
result: They observe a clear temporal sequence: energy first transfers from the gold surface to the molecule, then along the molecular backbone, with high thermal conductance across the junction.
conclusion: The study provides atomic-level insights into energy transport dynamics in molecular junctions, which may inform the design of efficient thermal interfaces.

title: Odd Elasticity In Disordered Chiral Active Materials
authors: Cheng-Tai Lee, Tom C. Lubensky, And Tomer Markovich
abstract:
Author(s): Cheng-Tai Lee, Tom C. Lubensky, and Tomer Markovich

A new theoretical framework for a chiral active solid allowing local internal rotations due to active torques shows how odd elasticity emerges in structurally-disordered materials relevant to biological and synthetic systems.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 038301] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for odd elasticity in disordered chiral active materials, focusing on mechanical properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how odd elasticity emerges in structurally-disordered chiral active materials, which are relevant to biological and synthetic systems.
method: The authors propose a new theoretical framework for chiral active solids that allows local internal rotations due to active torques.
result: The framework shows how odd elasticity can arise in disordered materials.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the mechanical behavior of chiral active materials but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quadratic Band Touching And Nontrivial Winding Reveal Generalized Angular Momentum Conservation
authors: Yihan Wang, Domenico Bongiovanni, Dario Jukić, Sihong Lei, Zhichan Hu, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Roberto Morandotti, Hrvoje Buljan, And Zhigang Chen
abstract:

Angular momentum conservation stands as one of the most fundamental and robust laws of physics. In discrete lattices, however, its realization can deviate markedly from the continuous case, especially in the presence of nontrivial momentum-space band touchings. Here, we investigate angular momentum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023803] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies angular momentum conservation in discrete lattices with quadratic band touching and nontrivial winding, revealing generalized angular momentum conservation laws.
motivation: Angular momentum conservation is fundamental in continuous systems, but its realization in discrete lattices can deviate, especially with nontrivial band touchings. The authors aim to understand these deviations.
method: The authors investigate a photonic lattice system with quadratic band touching and nontrivial winding, using theoretical analysis and experimental observations.
result: They discover generalized angular momentum conservation laws that account for the lattice structure and band topology.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of angular momentum conservation to discrete systems with nontrivial topology, relevant for photonic lattices and possibly other platforms.

title: Anyon Bound States And Hybrid Superconductivity
authors: Paul Leask
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Leask

The interactions of anyonic quasiparticles (vortices) in a Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory of the fractional quantum Hall effect is investigated and we show that it manifestly realizes a hybridization of type I or II superconductivity. Through Gauss’s law, each vortex simultaneously carries a fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anyon bound states in a Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory of the fractional quantum Hall effect and claims a hybridization of type I and II superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the interactions of anyonic quasiparticles in the fractional quantum Hall effect and their relation to superconductivity.
method: Theoretical analysis using Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory to model anyon interactions and derive bound states.
result: The model shows that anyon bound states lead to a hybridization of type I and type II superconductivity.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework linking anyonic quasiparticles to hybrid superconductivity in the fractional quantum Hall context.

title: Chiral Edge Excitations Of $ν=1/2$ Fractional Chern Insulators In The Bosonic Hofstadter Model
authors: Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, And Xiao-Yu Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, and Xiao-Yu Dong

Edge excitations are the defining signature of chiral topologically ordered systems. In continuum fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, these excitations are described by the chiral Luttinger liquid ([MATH]) theory. Whether these field theory predictions can be precisely identified in discre…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026504] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral edge excitations in fractional Chern insulators using the bosonic Hofstadter model.
motivation: To verify whether chiral Luttinger liquid theory predictions for edge excitations in fractional quantum Hall states hold in discrete lattice models of fractional Chern insulators.
method: Numerical simulations of the bosonic Hofstadter model at filling ν=1/2, analyzing edge state properties and comparing with field theory predictions.
result: The authors identify chiral edge excitations consistent with chiral Luttinger liquid theory, confirming the topological nature of the fractional Chern insulator.
conclusion: The bosonic Hofstadter model provides a lattice realization of fractional Chern insulators with chiral edge excitations described by known field theories.

title: Regge Trajectories From The Adjoint Sector Of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
authors: Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, And Pavel Meshcheriakov
abstract:
Author(s): Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, and Pavel Meshcheriakov

We reexamine the large [MATH] limit of [MATH] symmetric quantum mechanics of a Hermitian matrix whose singlet sector is well known to be exactly solvable via free fermions. When the Fermi level approaches a maximum of the potential, there is critical behavior corresponding to string theory in…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Regge trajectories in matrix quantum mechanics, connecting to string theory in AdS.
motivation: To understand the large N limit of matrix quantum mechanics and its critical behavior near a potential maximum, which relates to string theory.
method: Reexamines the singlet sector of Hermitian matrix quantum mechanics using free fermions and analyzes the spectrum near the potential maximum.
result: Finds Regge trajectories in the adjoint sector, indicating a connection to string theory in AdS.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the AdS/CFT correspondence and the emergence of stringy behavior from matrix models.

title: Unified First-Principles Formula For Time-Resolved Arpes Spectra Of Coherent And Incoherent Excitons Beyond The Dilute Limit
authors: Gianluca Stefanucci And Enrico Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): Gianluca Stefanucci and Enrico Perfetto

Despite major experimental progresses in time-resolved and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, a quantitative, microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced modifications of electronic band structures—applicable even beyond the low-density limit—is still lacking. Here, we close this …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026402] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles formula for time-resolved ARPES spectra of excitons beyond the dilute limit.
motivation: A quantitative microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced band structure modifications in time-resolved ARPES is lacking, especially beyond the low-density limit.
method: The authors derive a unified formula based on many-body perturbation theory, incorporating both coherent and incoherent exciton contributions.
result: The formula captures excitonic effects in photoemission spectra and is applicable to high exciton densities.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical tool for analyzing time-resolved ARPES experiments on excitonic systems.

title: Decoupled-Subspace-Induced Flat Bands In A Photonic Superlattice

Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, yet realizing flat dispersion across an entire Brillouin zone (BZ) remains nontrivial. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026902] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism to generate flat bands across the entire Brillouin zone in a photonic superlattice via decoupled subspaces.
motivation: Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, but achieving flat dispersion across the entire Brillouin zone is challenging.
method: The authors design a photonic superlattice where coupling between specific modes leads to decoupled subspaces, resulting in flat bands.
result: They demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that the proposed structure yields flat bands spanning the entire Brillouin zone.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to realizing broadband flat bands in photonic systems, with potential applications in light manipulation and nonlinear optics.

title: Tailoring Pure Valley-Zeeman Spin-Orbit Coupling In ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$-Encapsulated Monolayer Graphene
authors: Yaqing Han, Siqi Jiang, Jingkuan Xiao, Jiawei Jiang, Yulu Liu, Jiabei Huang, Yu Du, Di Zhang, Fuzhuo Lian, Wanting Xu, Siqin Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxiang Xi, Alexander S. Mayorov, Renjun Du, Kai Chang, Hongxin Yang, Lei Wang, And Geliang Yu

tldr: This paper studies valley-Zeeman spin-orbit coupling in WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene, focusing on Landau level reordering.
motivation: To understand the interplay between valley-Zeeman splitting and cyclotron energy in graphene heterostructures.
method: Magnetotransport measurements on WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene devices.
result: Observation of symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering due to competition between fixed valley-Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for controlling spin-orbit coupling in graphene, relevant for spintronics and valleytronics.

title: Wick Rotation Derivation For Weak Values Of The Density And Time-dependent Density Functional Theory
authors: Russell B. Thompson, Zarin Tasneem, And Yves Caudano
abstract:
Author(s): Russell B. Thompson, Zarin Tasneem, and Yves Caudano

The equations of time-dependent density functional theory are derived, via the expression for a quantum weak value, from ring polymer self-consistent-field theory using a mathematical correspondence between time and imaginary time. The imaginary-time path-integral formalism of Feynman, in which inve…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012206] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives time-dependent density functional theory from weak values using a Wick rotation correspondence, linking imaginary-time path integrals to real-time dynamics.
motivation: To provide a new derivation of time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) by connecting it to weak values and ring polymer self-consistent-field theory.
method: The authors use a mathematical correspondence between time and imaginary time (Wick rotation) to derive TDDFT equations from the expression for a quantum weak value within the imaginary-time path-integral formalism.
result: They show that TDDFT can be derived from weak values via Wick rotation, establishing a connection between these frameworks.
conclusion: The work offers a novel perspective on TDDFT but does not directly address the user's core research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Enantiosensitivity Of Spin Polarization In Molecular Photoionization
authors: Anton N. Artemyev, Daniel M. Haubenreißer, Boris M. Lagutin, And Philipp V. Demekhin
abstract:
