Angular distributions of photoelectrons with a defined spin orientation, released by the absorption of a single circularly polarized photon from randomly oriented chiral molecules, are derived and analyzed within the electric-dipole approximation. The revealed symmetry properties of the distribution…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013111] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin polarization in photoionization of chiral molecules, which is a topic in molecular physics and photoelectron spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the angular distribution of spin-polarized photoelectrons from chiral molecules, which is relevant to enantiosensitivity and molecular chirality detection.
method: The authors derive and analyze angular distributions of photoelectrons with defined spin orientation from randomly oriented chiral molecules within the electric-dipole approximation.
result: Symmetry properties of the distribution are revealed, showing enantiosensitive spin polarization effects.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for spin polarization in molecular photoionization, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Excitation-pulse Intensity Mediated Control Of Coherent Nonlinear Optical Response Of A V-type System
authors: Rishabh Tripathi, Krishna K. Maurya, And Rohan Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Rishabh Tripathi, Krishna K. Maurya, and Rohan Singh

V-type three-level systems, where two excited states share a common ground state, serve as fundamental models for exploring coherent light-matter interactions in a range of quantum systems, from atomic gases to semiconductor nanostructures. In this work, we investigate the coherent evolution of such…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013113] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent nonlinear optical response in a V-type three-level system controlled by excitation pulse intensity.
motivation: Understanding coherent light-matter interactions in V-type systems is fundamental for applications in atomic gases and semiconductor nanostructures.
method: The authors theoretically investigate the coherent evolution of a V-type system under varying excitation pulse intensities, analyzing the nonlinear optical response.
result: They demonstrate that the intensity of the excitation pulse can mediate control over the coherent nonlinear optical response.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling coherent dynamics in multilevel quantum systems, relevant for quantum optics and spectroscopy.

title: Temporal Coupled-mode Theory For A Single Floquet-sheet Resonator
authors: Yao-Ting Wang And Hsu-Hui Chou
abstract:
Author(s): Yao-Ting Wang and Hsu-Hui Chou

We develop a systematic temporal coupled-mode theory tailored for a single Floquet-sheet resonator governed by time-modulated conductivities. By invoking photon-number conservation during frequency conversion, we derive characteristic radiative decay rates and coupling coefficients that explicitly a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013511] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Develops a temporal coupled-mode theory for a single Floquet-sheet resonator with time-modulated conductivities.
motivation: To provide a systematic theoretical framework for analyzing resonators with time-varying properties, which are important for applications like frequency conversion and nonreciprocal devices.
method: Derives radiative decay rates and coupling coefficients by invoking photon-number conservation during frequency conversion within a temporal coupled-mode theory formalism.
result: Obtains explicit expressions for decay rates and coupling coefficients that account for the time-modulated conductivity of the Floquet-sheet resonator.
conclusion: The proposed theory enables accurate modeling of Floquet-sheet resonators, facilitating their design in photonic and quantum optical systems.

title: Generation Of Strongly Localized Skin Solitons In non-Hermitian Waveguide Arrays With The Kerr Effect
authors: Chong Hou, Boris A. Malomed, And Qin Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Chong Hou, Boris A. Malomed, and Qin Zhou

We address two distinct nonlinear propagation problems in nonlinear optical waveguide arrays (WGAs) with nonreciprocal (non-Hermitian) couplings. First, we investigate the light propagation launched by initial excitations of two different types. The single-channel excitation creates stable solitons …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013512] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear soliton propagation in non-Hermitian waveguide arrays with Kerr effect, focusing on optical physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand light propagation and soliton formation in non-Hermitian waveguide arrays with nonlinearity, which is a topic in classical nonlinear optics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two nonlinear propagation problems in waveguide arrays with nonreciprocal couplings, using numerical simulations and analytical methods.
result: They find that single-channel excitation creates stable solitons, and they characterize the properties of these localized skin solitons.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of nonlinear wave dynamics in non-Hermitian systems, but has no direct connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Kerr-induced Orbital Handedness Birefringence Of Optical Vortex Modes In Optical Fibers
authors: Chang Kyun Ha, Eun Mi Kim, And Vishwatosh Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Kyun Ha, Eun Mi Kim, and Vishwatosh Mishra

Birefringence is commonly associated with anisotropic or chiral media, but optical nonlinearity can also induce effective symmetry breaking, enabling circular birefringence even in isotropic materials through helicity-dependent Kerr phase shifts. Extending this concept to the orbital angular momentu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013513] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kerr-induced orbital handedness birefringence of optical vortex modes in optical fibers, a nonlinear optics phenomenon.
motivation: To extend the concept of circular birefringence from spin angular momentum to orbital angular momentum in isotropic media via Kerr nonlinearity.
method: Theoretical analysis of Kerr-induced phase shifts for optical vortex modes in optical fibers, deriving conditions for orbital handedness birefringence.
result: Demonstrates that orbital handedness birefringence can occur due to Kerr effect, leading to differential propagation of left- and right-handed optical vortices.
conclusion: This work reveals a new type of birefringence in optical fibers, with potential applications in all-optical switching and vortex mode manipulation.

title: Controllable Temporal Reflection And Refraction Via Coupling Phase Engineering
authors: Yurong Liu, Chengqi Wu, Hanxiao Zhang, And Chuhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yurong Liu, Chengqi Wu, Hanxiao Zhang, and Chuhui Fan

Temporal boundary effects provide a potential route to treat time as an additional degree of freedom in the design of optical devices, while a key challenge in this context is the controllable manipulation of temporal reflection and refraction components. In this work, we demonstrate that the abrupt…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013509] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controllable temporal reflection and refraction via coupling phase engineering in optical systems.
motivation: Temporal boundary effects offer a new degree of freedom for optical device design, but controllable manipulation of temporal reflection and refraction remains challenging.
method: The authors use abrupt changes in coupling phase to induce temporal boundaries and analyze the resulting reflection and refraction components.
result: They achieve controllable temporal reflection and refraction, demonstrating the ability to manipulate light in the time domain.
conclusion: Coupling phase engineering provides a viable route for controlling temporal boundary effects, with potential applications in optical devices.

title: Quantum Stochastic Dynamics Of Nonlinear Driven Light Emission
authors: Philipp Stammer
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Stammer

This work extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation towards open systems, by considering a quantum stochastic analysis of the field modes coupled to an environment. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 013712] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation to open systems using quantum stochastic dynamics.
motivation: To understand the open system dynamics of nonlinear driven light emission, which is relevant for high harmonic generation.
method: Solves the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an environment.
result: Provides a quantum stochastic analysis of the field modes and their interaction with the environment.
conclusion: The work offers a framework for studying open system effects in high harmonic generation.

title: Mechanisms Of Enantiosensitivity In Rescattering Photoelectron Spectroscopy
authors: Kirill V. Bazarov And Oleg I. Tolstikhin
abstract:
Author(s): Kirill V. Bazarov and Oleg I. Tolstikhin

It was shown that in rescattering photoelectron spectroscopy of chiral molecules, the enantiosensitive signal splits into two stage-resolved contributions from tunneling and rescattering. They can be controlled independently by varying the relative phase of an orthogonal two-color field.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011101] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies enantiosensitivity in rescattering photoelectron spectroscopy of chiral molecules using orthogonal two-color fields.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms of enantiosensitivity in photoelectron spectroscopy can help distinguish chiral molecules, which is important in chemistry and biology.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the rescattering photoelectron spectroscopy signal and decompose it into contributions from tunneling and rescattering, controlled by the relative phase of an orthogonal two-color field.
result: The enantiosensitive signal splits into two stage-resolved contributions that can be independently controlled.
conclusion: The findings provide a way to control enantiosensitivity in photoelectron spectroscopy, but the work is focused on molecular physics and spectroscopy, not on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hyperfine Spectroscopy And Laser Cooling Of The Fermionic Isotopes $^{47}\mathrm{Ti}$ And $^{49}\mathrm{Ti}$
authors: Jackson Schrott, Scott Eustice, Pouya Sadeghpour, Rowan Duim, Hiromitsu Sawaoka, Dmytro Filin, Marianna S. Safronova, And Dan M. Stamper-Kurn

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012806] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical trapping and hyperfine spectroscopy of fermionic titanium isotopes.
motivation: Laser cooling and trapping of fermionic isotopes with nonzero nuclear spin is challenging due to hyperfine structure; this work extends atomic cooling to new species.
method: The authors perform hyperfine spectroscopy and demonstrate magneto-optical trapping of 47Ti and 49Ti using laser cooling techniques.
result: Successful trapping and characterization of hyperfine structure for both isotopes.
conclusion: Fermionic titanium isotopes can be laser-cooled and trapped, enabling future studies in quantum simulation or precision measurement.

title: Long-lived Oscillations Of An Attractive Polaron In A Bose Gas
authors: Saptarshi Majumdar And Aleksandra Petković

Author(s): Dmitry V. Chichinadze

The nonlinear transport regime is manifested in the nonlinear current-voltage characteristic of the system. An example of such a nonlinear regime is a setup in which current is injected into the sample and the measured voltage drop is quadratic in the injected current. Such a quadratic nonlinear reg…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065413] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies weak localization and antilocalization corrections to nonlinear transport in disordered systems using a semiclassical Boltzmann approach.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear transport is important for characterizing electronic properties of materials, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The author develops a semiclassical Boltzmann treatment to compute weak localization and antilocalization corrections to the nonlinear current-voltage characteristic.
result: The paper derives analytical expressions for the nonlinear transport coefficients and discusses the crossover between weak localization and antilocalization.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for nonlinear transport in disordered systems, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nanobubble Superstructure: A Tuneable Grid Of Molecule Clusters In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Liye Fu, Yuerui Lu, And Juan F. Torres
abstract:
Author(s): Liye Fu, Yuerui Lu, and Juan F. Torres

Highly dense and ordered nanobubble arrays in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are crucial for strain engineering electronic devices, fabricating high-capacity energy storage systems, and creating quantum emitters. However, neighboring nanobubbles have been found to spontaneously coalesce becaus…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065414] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of a nanobubble superstructure in twisted bilayer graphene, enabling a tuneable grid of molecule clusters.
motivation: Highly dense and ordered nanobubble arrays are crucial for strain engineering, energy storage, and quantum emitters, but coalescence has been a challenge.
method: The authors demonstrate a method to create and stabilize a nanobubble superstructure in twisted bilayer graphene, likely through controlled annealing or strain engineering.
result: A tuneable grid of molecule clusters is achieved, with potential applications in quantum emitters and strain engineering.
conclusion: The nanobubble superstructure provides a new platform for quantum emitters and strain engineering in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of Indistinguishable Energy States And The Glass Transition
authors: Shimul Akhanjee
abstract:
Author(s): Shimul Akhanjee

The statistical mechanics of particles that populate indistinguishable energy substates is explored. In particular, the mathematical treatment of microstates differs from conventional statistical mechanics, where, for a given degeneracy, the energy sublevels or substates are universally treated as d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014119] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a modified statistical mechanics for indistinguishable energy substates to model the glass transition.
motivation: Standard statistical mechanics treats degenerate energy levels as distinct, which may not capture the physics of glasses where substates are indistinguishable.
method: The author develops a formalism where microstates are counted differently when energy substates are indistinguishable, altering the partition function.
result: The new counting leads to a different thermodynamic behavior that exhibits a glass transition-like singularity.
conclusion: Indistinguishability of energy states may be a key ingredient in understanding the glass transition from first principles.

title: Twisted State Stability Under Local Order Parameter Adaptation
authors: Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, And Ya Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, and Ya Jia

Twisted states commonly arise in nonlocally coupled ring networks. We study the stability of twisted states in networks with higher-order interactions under the adaptive mechanism based on the local order parameter. The adaptive feedback dynamically regulates the coupling strength and thus reshapes …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014209] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of twisted states in nonlocally coupled ring networks with higher-order interactions and adaptive coupling based on local order parameters.
motivation: Twisted states are common in coupled oscillator networks, and understanding their stability under adaptive mechanisms is important for controlling synchronization patterns.
method: The authors analyze a ring network of phase oscillators with higher-order (simplicial) interactions and introduce adaptive feedback that adjusts coupling strengths based on the local order parameter. They perform linear stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: They derive stability conditions for twisted states and show that the adaptive mechanism can stabilize or destabilize certain twisted states depending on parameters.
conclusion: The adaptive coupling based on local order parameter provides a way to control twisted state stability in networks with higher-order interactions.

title: Energy-dynamics Interplay In Temporal Networks Triggers Explosive Synchronization
authors: Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, And Thierry Njougouo
abstract:
Author(s): Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, and Thierry Njougouo

Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in the study of collective behavior. In this paper we investigate the synchronization transition in networks of coupled dynamical systems from an energetic perspective. Interactions between systems/oscillators are assumed to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive synchronization in temporal networks from an energetic perspective, focusing on coupled oscillators.
motivation: Understanding synchronization transitions in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in collective behavior.
method: The authors model interactions between oscillators with an energy-based coupling and analyze the synchronization transition using numerical simulations.
result: They find that the interplay between energy dynamics and temporal network structure triggers explosive synchronization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into synchronization phenomena but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Nanorotator In The Hypomagnetic Field: Implications For Magnetobiology
authors: V. N. Binhi
abstract:
Author(s): V. N. Binhi

A mechanism for the biological effects of the hypomagnetic field is proposed, based on the rotational motion of a molecule as a whole within a cavity in an enzyme. It has been shown previously that a molecular rotator about 1 nm in size can have a decoherence time of up to tens of milliseconds. On s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014406] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum nanorotator mechanism for biological effects of hypomagnetic fields.
motivation: To explain how weak magnetic fields can affect biological systems via quantum rotational dynamics.
method: Models a molecular rotator in an enzyme cavity with decoherence times up to tens of milliseconds.
result: The rotator's quantum behavior may be influenced by hypomagnetic fields, leading to biological effects.
conclusion: Quantum nanorotators could mediate magnetobiological effects, but the mechanism remains speculative.

title: Hamiltonian Active Particles In Incompressible Fluid Membranes
authors: Sneha Krishnan And Rickmoy Samanta
abstract:
Author(s): Sneha Krishnan and Rickmoy Samanta

Active proteins and membrane-bound motors exert force dipole flows along fluid interfaces and lipid bilayers. We develop a Hamiltonian framework for the interactions of pusher and puller dipoles embedded in an incompressible two-dimensional membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase. Beginning…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015102] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: A Hamiltonian framework for active particles in incompressible fluid membranes.
motivation: To understand interactions of active proteins and membrane-bound motors in biological membranes.
method: Develops a Hamiltonian formalism for pusher and puller dipoles in a 2D incompressible membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase.
result: Derives equations of motion and interaction potentials for the active dipoles.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical basis for studying active particle dynamics in fluid membranes.

title: Structure And Memory Control Self-diffusion In Active Matter
authors: Akinlade Akintunde And Stewart A. Mallory
abstract:
Author(s): Akinlade Akintunde and Stewart A. Mallory

Despite extensive progress in characterizing the emergent behavior of active matter, the microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a framework that quantitatively links self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014115] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a framework linking self-diffusion in active matter to collisional forces and their temporal correlations.
motivation: The microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems are poorly understood despite progress in characterizing emergent behavior.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that quantitatively connects self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correlations.
result: The framework provides a quantitative link between self-diffusion and collisional forces in active matter.
conclusion: The study advances understanding of self-diffusion in active matter from a microscopic perspective.

title: Information Temperature And Macroscopic Descriptors Of Additive $N\text{th}$-order Markov Chains
authors: O. V. Usatenko, G. M. Pritula, And S. S. Melnyk
abstract:
Author(s): O. V. Usatenko, G. M. Pritula, and S. S. Melnyk

Large-scale language models (LLMs) operate in extremely high-dimensional state spaces, where both token embeddings and their hidden representations create complex dependences that are not easily reduced to classical Markov structures. In this paper we explore a theoretically solvable approximation o…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014116] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a solvable Markov chain model to approximate high-dimensional dependencies in LLMs, defining an 'information temperature' and macroscopic descriptors.
motivation: Large language models operate in extremely high-dimensional spaces with complex dependencies that are not easily captured by classical Markov models; a tractable approximation is needed.
method: The authors propose an additive Nth-order Markov chain as a simplified model and derive information-theoretic quantities such as entropy rate and information temperature.
result: They obtain closed-form expressions for macroscopic descriptors and show how the information temperature characterizes the model's statistical properties.
conclusion: The model provides a useful approximation for understanding dependencies in LLMs, but its direct applicability to real LLMs remains limited.

title: Topological Transitions In Swarmalators Systems
authors: Patrick Louodop, Michael N. Jipdi, Gael R. Simo, Steve J. Kongni, Carmel Lambu, Thierry Njougouo, Pablo D. Mininni, Kevin O'keeffe, And Hilda A. Cerdeira
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Louodop, Michael N. Jipdi, Gael R. Simo, Steve J. Kongni, Carmel Lambu, Thierry Njougouo, Pablo D. Mininni, Kevin O'Keeffe, and Hilda A. Cerdeira

After its development, the swarmalators model attracted a great deal of attention since it was found to be very suitable to reproduce several behaviors in collective dynamics. However, few works explain the transitions that are observed while varying system parameters. In this letter, we demonstrate…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012201] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions in swarmalator systems, which are models of collective dynamics combining synchronization and swarming.
motivation: Understanding the transitions observed in swarmalator systems as parameters vary is important for explaining collective behaviors in nature.
method: The authors analyze a swarmalator model and demonstrate topological transitions through numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They identify and characterize topological transitions in the system's collective dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase transitions of swarmalator systems, contributing to the field of collective dynamics.

title: Percolation And Criticality Of Systems With Competing Interactions On Bethe Lattices: Limitations And Potential Strengths Of Cluster Schemes
authors: Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, And Marco Tarzia
abstract:
Author(s): Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, and Marco Tarzia

Cluster-based algorithms have led to remarkably efficient Monte Carlo sampling schemes that reduce critical slowing down. The authors demonstrate that seeking such cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, but they leave open the possibility that alternate approaches could be devised.

#TechnicalAdvancement #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014114] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation and criticality in frustrated systems on Bethe lattices, demonstrating the limitations of cluster Monte Carlo algorithms.
motivation: Cluster algorithms reduce critical slowing down in Monte Carlo simulations, but their effectiveness for frustrated systems is unclear.
method: The authors analyze cluster schemes for systems with competing interactions on Bethe lattices, using theoretical and numerical approaches.
result: They show that cluster algorithms fail for frustrated systems due to frustration-induced barriers, but suggest alternative approaches might exist.
conclusion: Seeking cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, though alternate methods could be devised.

title: Stability Of Delay-coupled Reaction-diffusion Systems With Turing Or Wave Instability
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, and Naoyuki Hara

A quenching phenomenon that emerges in coupled oscillators, namely, amplitude death (AD), has been widely accepted. The present paper analytically deals with AD in two identical reaction-diffusion systems with periodic boundary or zero-flux boundary conditions that are coupled by a diffusive connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014207] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death in delay-coupled reaction-diffusion systems with Turing or wave instability.
motivation: Understanding amplitude death in coupled oscillators is important for controlling oscillations in biological and chemical systems.
method: The authors analytically investigate two identical reaction-diffusion systems coupled by diffusive connections under periodic or zero-flux boundary conditions.
result: They derive conditions for amplitude death and analyze the effects of delay and coupling strength.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into quenching phenomena in spatially extended systems with time delays.

title: Riding The Wave: Polymers In Time-dependent Nonequilibrium Baths
authors: Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, And Abhinav Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, and Abhinav Sharma

Directed transport is a characteristic feature of numerous biological systems in response to signals such as nutrient and chemical gradients. These signals often depend on time owing to the high complexity of interactions in these systems. In this study, we focus on the steady-state behavior of poly…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies directed transport of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, focusing on steady-state behavior.
motivation: Understanding directed transport in biological systems where signals are time-dependent due to complex interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis of polymer dynamics in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, likely using stochastic thermodynamics or polymer physics.
result: Steady-state behavior of polymers under time-dependent driving is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides insights into polymer transport in complex biological environments but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: From Active To Odd To Smart Matter
authors: Olivier Dauchot
abstract:
Author(s): Olivier Dauchot

Active matter taught us that microscopic energy injection can lead to macroscopic dynamical order. Odd elasticity revealed that active solids can turn deformation into work. The next question is sharper: can matter learn what it is good for?


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 011001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the evolution of active matter research towards 'smart matter' that can learn and adapt.
motivation: To explore the next frontier in active matter where materials can learn and perform useful functions.
method: Conceptual review and forward-looking perspective based on recent developments in active matter and odd elasticity.
result: Proposes the idea of 'smart matter' that can learn from its environment and adapt its behavior.
conclusion: The field is moving from understanding active and odd matter to creating materials that can learn and optimize their responses.

title: Model-free Analysis Of Complex Systems Using Delayed-feedback Echo State Network
authors: Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, And Xu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, and Xu Xu

Investigating the dynamical behavior of complex systems from data poses formidable challenges in the field of nonlinear science. This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network ( df-ESN) model specifically designed for modeling and analyzing complex systems from data. The df-ESN introdu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014204] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network for modeling complex dynamical systems from data.
motivation: Modeling complex systems from data is challenging; existing methods may not capture long-range dependencies.
method: A delayed-feedback echo state network (df-ESN) is introduced, incorporating time-delayed connections to improve memory.
result: The df-ESN demonstrates improved prediction accuracy on benchmark chaotic systems compared to standard ESN.
conclusion: Delayed feedback enhances the modeling capability of reservoir computing for complex systems.

title: Interaction Of Solitons With Saturable Gain
authors: Akhilesh K. S. And Omri Gat
abstract:
Author(s): Akhilesh K. S. and Omri Gat

We study the tail-overlap interaction of a well-separated pair of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain. Gain saturation introduces nonlocal terms in the soliton field equation that depend on the total energy and therefore invalidate the standard methods used to study overlap inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014205] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the interaction of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain, focusing on tail-overlap effects.
motivation: Understanding soliton interactions is important for nonlinear optics and laser dynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating nonlocal gain saturation terms and analyze the interaction dynamics.
result: They find that gain saturation introduces nonlocal effects that modify the standard soliton interaction picture.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of dissipative solitons but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Eigenvector Localization And Universal Regime Transitions In Multiplex Networks: A Perturbative Approach
authors: Joan Hernàndez Tey And Emanuele Cozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Hernàndez Tey and Emanuele Cozzo

We study the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in a general contact-based contagion model on multiplex networks. Using the inverse participation ratio, we characterize how activity shifts from being confined to a single layer to spreading across the entire system. Through a …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014307] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies eigenvector localization and regime transitions in multiplex networks using a perturbative approach, applied to contagion models.
motivation: Understanding how activity localizes in multiplex networks is important for modeling contagion processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the inverse participation ratio and perturbation theory to analyze the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in multiplex networks.
result: They characterize the transition and show how activity shifts from single-layer to whole-system spreading.
conclusion: The work provides insights into multiplex network dynamics but is unrelated to the specified research interests.

title: Effect Of Higher-order Interactions On Noisy Majority-rule Dynamics With Random Group Sizes
authors: Roni Muslim, Jong-Min Park, Jihye Kim, And Rinto Anugraha NQZ
abstract:
Author(s): Roni Muslim, Jong-Min Park, Jihye Kim, and Rinto Anugraha NQZ

We study opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions, motivated by the fact that social influence often takes place in groups rather than only through pairwise contacts. We introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and investigate how the distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014308] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions using a noisy majority-rule model on hypergraphs.
motivation: Social influence often occurs in groups, not just pairwise contacts, motivating the study of higher-order interactions in opinion dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and analyze the effect of group size distribution on the dynamics.
result: The distribution of group sizes significantly affects the phase transition and consensus behavior of the model.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and group size heterogeneity are important for understanding opinion formation in social systems.

title: Segregation Dynamics In Active-passive Mixtures Of Semiflexible Filaments
authors: Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, And Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract:
Author(s): Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, and Sriram Ramaswamy

We study the segregation of motile semiflexible filaments from a background of similar but nonmotile filaments. Our Langevin dynamics simulations reveal a wide range of emergent structures governed by filament flexibility and activity, i.e., self-propulsion strength. The system segregates at low act…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015405] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies segregation dynamics in mixtures of active and passive semiflexible filaments using Langevin dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding how activity and flexibility govern structure formation in active-passive mixtures is important for biological and soft matter systems.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of semiflexible filaments with varying flexibility and self-propulsion strength.
result: The system segregates at low activity, forming clusters and bands; flexibility modulates the emergent structures.
conclusion: Activity and flexibility jointly determine segregation patterns in active-passive filament mixtures.

title: Hyperuniformity Near Jamming Transition Over A Wide Range Of Bidispersity
authors: Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, And Kunimasa Miyazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, and Kunimasa Miyazaki

Hyperuniformity, the anomalous suppression of density fluctuations in dense particle systems, has been reported in amorphous solids near the jamming transition. This manuscript shows that the value of the hyperuniformity scaling exponent in two dimensions differs from that in three dimensions, unlike previously thought.

#AdvancingField #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hyperuniformity scaling exponents near the jamming transition in bidisperse particle systems, finding a difference between 2D and 3D.
motivation: Hyperuniformity is a property of dense particle systems where density fluctuations are anomalously suppressed, and it has been observed near jamming. The authors aim to clarify whether the scaling exponent is universal across dimensions.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of bidisperse particle systems in 2D and 3D, analyzing density fluctuations and extracting hyperuniformity scaling exponents.
result: They find that the hyperuniformity scaling exponent in 2D differs from that in 3D, contradicting previous assumptions of universality.
conclusion: The hyperuniformity exponent is not universal across dimensions, indicating a more complex dependence on dimensionality and bidispersity.

title: Phase Transitions In The Lieb-kagome Lattice Interpolation
authors: T. F. O. Lara, R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): T. F. O. Lara, R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We study the ferromagnetic Ising model on a two-dimensional transition lattice that continuously interpolates between the Lieb and kagome lattices via a geometric deformation parameterized by the angle [MATH]. The exchange couplings follow a distance-dependent decay controlled by an exponent [MATH], enabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014111] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in the ferromagnetic Ising model on a lattice interpolating between Lieb and kagome geometries.
motivation: To understand how lattice geometry affects critical behavior in statistical mechanical models.
method: Analytical and numerical methods for the Ising model on a tunable lattice with distance-dependent exchange couplings.
result: Identifies phase transition properties as a function of the geometric deformation parameter.
conclusion: The interpolation reveals how lattice structure influences phase transitions, but the work is purely classical statistical mechanics without quantum information or thermodynamics connections.

title: Sufficient Statistics For Parameter Inference In The Stochastic Van Der Pol Oscillator Model For Thermoacoustic Instabilities
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Sungtaek Ju

Thermoacoustic instabilities pose a critical challenge in the design and operation of many combustion systems. We report a low-dimensional statistics approach for inferring the parameters of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator from trajectory observations. From the exponential family structure of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014203] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a low-dimensional statistics approach for parameter inference in stochastic Van der Pol oscillators modeling thermoacoustic instabilities.
motivation: Thermoacoustic instabilities are a critical challenge in combustion systems, and accurate parameter inference from trajectory data is needed.
method: The authors exploit the exponential family structure of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator to derive sufficient statistics for parameter estimation.
result: A low-dimensional statistics approach is reported that enables efficient parameter inference from trajectory observations.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for inferring parameters of thermoacoustic instability models.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki
abstract:
Author(s): Zsófia Simon and Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the activity-driven temporal network model to incorporate spatiotemporal constraints, analyzing how spatial embedding affects spreading dynamics.
motivation: Many real temporal networks, such as physical proximity networks, are embedded in space, but existing activity-driven models ignore spatial aspects. The authors aim to understand how spatial constraints influence dynamical processes on temporal networks.
method: The authors introduce a spatiotemporal activity-driven model where nodes are placed in a metric space and connections depend on both activity and spatial distance. They derive analytical expressions for the temporal network's structural properties and simulate spreading processes.
result: The model reveals that spatial embedding can significantly slow down spreading and alter the epidemic threshold compared to the non-spatial activity-driven model. The analytical predictions match simulations well.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal constraints are crucial for accurately modeling real-world temporal networks, and the proposed model provides a tractable framework for studying spreading dynamics in such systems.

title: Neural Optimization Of The Most Probable Paths Of Three-dimensional Active Brownian Particles
authors: Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, And Shigeyuki Komura
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, and Shigeyuki Komura

By minimizing the Onsager-Machlup integral with a neural-network framework, this Letter determines the most probable paths of a three-dimensional active Brownian particle. These optimal transition pathways exhibit distinct geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes. The work provides a versatile framework for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

#WellStructured #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012103] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a neural-network framework to find most probable paths of active Brownian particles in 3D, revealing helical transition pathways.
motivation: Understanding optimal transition pathways in active matter systems is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, but the paper focuses on classical active particles rather than quantum systems.
method: The Onsager-Machlup integral is minimized using a neural-network approach to determine the most probable paths of a three-dimensional active Brownian particle.
result: Optimal transition pathways exhibit geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes, demonstrating the versatility of the neural-network framework.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems, but it does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Can Machine Learning Truly Decode Phase Transitions? A Deep Dive Into The Ising Model With Competing Interactions
authors: Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, And David P. Landau
abstract:
Author(s): Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, and David P. Landau

The authors investigate phase transitions in the two-dimensional Ising model with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions, by combining machine learning with simulations and finite-size scaling. The results show that machine learning can decode ordering patterns, extract order-parameter analogs, and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.

#MachineLearningSpotlight #TimelyTopic


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014104] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to study phase transitions in the 2D Ising model with competing interactions, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test whether machine learning can decode ordering patterns and extract order parameters in frustrated Ising systems.
method: Combines machine learning (likely neural networks) with Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling to analyze the 2D Ising model with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: Machine learning can reproduce critical behavior and extract order-parameter analogs in frustrated Ising systems.
conclusion: Machine learning is a useful tool for studying phase transitions in classical spin systems with competing interactions.

title: Tunable Bands In One-dimensional Fractional Quantum Media
authors: Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, And Lincoln D. Carr
abstract:
Author(s): Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, and Lincoln D. Carr

Fractional calculus has become an essential framework in geophysics, optics, and biological systems to capture long-range correlations and anomalous transport. In this article, we extend the success of fractional calculus in physical models to explore a particle in a periodic potential, where the Sc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014106] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a particle in a periodic potential using fractional calculus to capture long-range correlations and anomalous transport.
motivation: Fractional calculus is widely used in geophysics, optics, and biology, and the authors aim to extend its application to periodic potentials in quantum systems.
method: The authors apply fractional calculus to model a particle in a one-dimensional periodic potential, analyzing the resulting band structure.
result: They find tunable bands in fractional quantum media, demonstrating the effect of fractional derivatives on the energy spectrum.
conclusion: Fractional calculus provides a new tool for understanding quantum systems with long-range correlations, but the work is primarily a mathematical extension without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effects Of Quenched Disorder In Three-dimensional Lattice ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Gauge Higgs Models
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We study the effects of uncorrelated quenched disorder to the phase diagram and continuous transitions of three-dimensional lattice [MATH] gauge Higgs models. For this purpose, we consider two types of quenched disorder, associated with the sites and plaquettes of the cubic lattice. In b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014107] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effects of quenched disorder on phase transitions in three-dimensional lattice Z2 gauge Higgs models.
motivation: Understanding how disorder affects phase diagrams and critical behavior in gauge theories is important for condensed matter and high-energy physics.
method: The authors consider two types of quenched disorder (site and plaquette) and analyze the phase diagram and continuous transitions using numerical simulations or analytical methods.
result: The presence of quenched disorder modifies the phase diagram and may change the nature of phase transitions.
conclusion: Quenched disorder has significant effects on the critical properties of three-dimensional Z2 gauge Higgs models.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler
abstract:
Author(s): L. A. Rüffert and T. E. Mehlstäubler

Self-organized three-dimensional (3D) ion Coulomb crystals in linear Paul traps naturally form concentric shells that provide a curved, atomically resolved interface for studying two-dimensional (2D) nanofriction. Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical many-body physics and nanofriction, not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at curved interfaces using self-organized ion crystals.
method: Experimental and theoretical study of 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap, observing shell structures and measuring friction.
result: Observation of concentric shells and characterization of two-dimensional nanofriction.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals provide a platform for studying nanofriction, but the work does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, and Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. Here, we uncover a Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets: interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light irradiation can selectively polarize Kramers partnered states allowing to control …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where circularly polarized light selectively polarizes Kramers partnered states.
conclusion: This effect provides a mechanism to control Kramers pairs, which may have applications in spintronics or optoelectronics, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Virgile Troude and Didier Sornette

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. Here, we show that such behavior can emerge far from instability through a universal mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that heavy-tailed fluctuations can arise from non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: To explain the origin of heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics observed in various fields without invoking criticality.
method: The authors analyze multidimensional Kesten processes and identify a mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification that generates heavy tails.
result: Heavy-tailed behavior emerges from non-normal amplification even when the system is far from instability, providing a universal mechanism.
conclusion: Non-normal eigenvector amplification is a robust mechanism for heavy-tailed fluctuations, applicable across physics, finance, and economics.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú and Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

Artificial colloidal ice is an icelike system used to study the effects of frustration in controlled environments, where all degrees of freedom can be accessed at a length scale large enough for optical visualization and in real time. We modify this model system by inducing anisotropic interactions …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in an artificial colloidal ice system with anisotropic interactions, focusing on frustration and real-time dynamics.
motivation: To understand the effects of frustration in controlled environments by modifying artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions.
method: The authors induce anisotropic interactions in an artificial colloidal ice system and observe the resulting dynamics using optical visualization.
result: Anisotropic interactions lead to dynamical spin freezing, where the system exhibits slow relaxation and frozen spin configurations.
conclusion: Anisotropic interactions can induce dynamical freezing in frustrated systems, providing insights into non-equilibrium dynamics in artificial spin ice.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules
authors: Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, And Salvador Miret-Artés
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, and Salvador Miret-Artés

We propose a theoretical mechanism to indirectly detect the small parity-violating energy difference (PVED) between chiral enantiomers through a macroscopic enantiomeric excess observed in an ultracold gas. We consider that chiral molecules are formed resonantly via ultracold collisions of achiral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033056] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical mechanism to detect parity violation in chiral molecules via ultracold gas amplification.
motivation: Parity-violating energy differences between enantiomers are extremely small and have never been directly observed; the paper aims to amplify this effect to detectable levels.
method: The authors model ultracold collisions of achiral atoms to form chiral molecules resonantly, and show that a small PVED can lead to a macroscopic enantiomeric excess under certain conditions.
result: The mechanism predicts that an initial tiny PVED can be amplified into a measurable enantiomeric excess in an ultracold gas.
conclusion: This provides a new avenue for detecting parity violation in molecular systems, though it remains theoretical and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees
authors: Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, And Tomáš Bzdušek
abstract:
Author(s): Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, and Tomáš Bzdušek

We derive the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that constitute tree analogs of selected two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, namely, the Lieb, the double-Lieb, the kagome, and the star lattice. The common feature of these Euclidean lattices is that their nearest-neighbor models give rise to fl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033036] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that are tree analogs of certain two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, revealing flat bands and topological states.
motivation: To understand the spectral properties and topological features of tree-like lattices that mimic the Lieb, kagome, and star lattices.
method: Exact diagonalization and analytical solution of tight-binding models on decorated Cayley trees.
result: The spectra exhibit flat bands and topological edge states analogous to those in the Euclidean counterparts.
conclusion: Decorated Cayley trees serve as tractable models for studying flat bands and topology in non-Euclidean geometries.

title: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales
authors: Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, And Nicole Abaid
abstract:
Author(s): Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, and Nicole Abaid

Collective motion in active matter can arise from interaction rules that generate group-level order. A seminal example is the Vicsek model, which describes flocking using a simple local alignment rule. Despite three decades of research, the network topology induced by the particles’ alignment remain…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion across scales.
motivation: Understanding how local alignment rules lead to group-level order in active matter systems is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze the network topology induced by particle alignment in the Vicsek model, examining cluster properties across different scales.
result: They characterize the topological and geometric features of clusters, revealing scale-dependent behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the structure of collective motion but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emergence Of Bistability And Even-order Harmonic Generation In A Centrosymmetric System Under Periodic Driving
authors: Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, And Ryo Shimano
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, and Ryo Shimano

Nonequilibrium states of matter, when driven periodically, can exhibit exotic properties and emergent behaviors that are fundamentally distinct from those in equilibrium systems. To investigate the dynamical behavior of a particle system under time-periodic external forces, we performed numerical si…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033041] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system under periodic driving, using numerical simulations.
motivation: To explore emergent nonequilibrium behaviors in periodically driven systems that are distinct from equilibrium.
method: Numerical simulations of a particle system under time-periodic external forces.
result: Observation of bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce exotic properties like bistability and even-order harmonics in centrosymmetric systems.

title: Quantum Physics-informed Neural Network With Residual-based Adaptive Refinement For Solving Partial Differential Equations
authors: Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, And Zhichao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, and Zhichao Zhang

In this paper, we propose a quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by using residual-based adaptive refinement (RAR). The method incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism into the training of QPINN, which aims to enhance conver…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033042] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum physics-informed neural network with residual-based adaptive refinement for solving partial differential equations.
motivation: To improve the convergence and accuracy of quantum neural networks for solving PDEs by adaptively sampling points with high residual error.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that uses a parameterized quantum circuit as the neural network and incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism (RAR) to focus training on regions with large PDE residuals.
result: The method demonstrates improved convergence and accuracy compared to standard QPINNs on benchmark PDEs, with fewer required collocation points.
conclusion: Residual-based adaptive refinement enhances the performance of quantum physics-informed neural networks for solving PDEs, showing potential for quantum advantage in scientific computing.

title: Particle-hole Origin Of Thermal Beating In Dipole-compression Modes Of A One-dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, And Giulia de Rosi
abstract:
Author(s): Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, and Giulia De Rosi

This work reports a beating signal of two dipole-compression collective mode frequencies evolving from the low-temperature phononic hydrodynamic regime to the collisionless limit at the hole-induced anomaly temperature. The lower (higher) frequency originates from hole (particle) spectral states, and the temperature dependence of their relative excitation strengths reflects the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032003] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal beating in dipole-compression modes of a 1D Bose gas, attributing it to particle-hole spectral states.
motivation: Understanding collective mode behavior in ultracold gases across temperature regimes is important for many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the temperature dependence of two dipole-compression mode frequencies using a particle-hole picture and compare with experimental data.
result: They find that the lower frequency originates from hole states and the higher from particle states, with relative excitation strengths reflecting thermal population imbalance.
conclusion: The beating signal arises from the interplay of particle and hole excitations, providing insight into the crossover from hydrodynamic to collisionless regimes.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling To Model Lagrangian Tracer Dispersion In Turbulent Boundary Layer
authors: Fabian Schindler And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Schindler and Jörg Schumacher

We present a quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QE-MCMC) method to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution that depends on all three components and height to model the transport and dispersion of massless Lagrangian tracer particles in two different turbulent s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033031] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layers.
motivation: Turbulent dispersion of tracer particles is important for environmental and engineering applications, but classical MCMC sampling can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors propose a quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm that uses a quantum computer to accelerate sampling from the joint target distribution of turbulent acceleration vectors.
result: The quantum-enhanced method shows improved sampling efficiency compared to classical MCMC for the specific turbulent flow configurations studied.
conclusion: Quantum computing can offer advantages for certain computational fluid dynamics problems, but the work is primarily an application of quantum algorithms to classical fluid dynamics.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, focusing on biomolecular condensates near membranes.
motivation: Understanding how surfaces affect phase separation in cells is important for biology but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically model phase separation under finite molecule number constraints in a confined geometry.
result: They find that surface phase separation behavior is modified by confinement and finite-size effects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into biological condensates but does not connect to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Extracting dynamic properties from quantum Monte Carlo simulations requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed. The maximum entropy method is a common approach, but its behavior in limiting cases is not well understood.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the maximum entropy method in the noiseless limit and the improved-prior limit, and test these predictions on synthetic data.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the method recovers the exact spectral function, while the improved-prior limit yields a biased but smooth reconstruction. They also discuss implications for practical analytic continuation.
conclusion: The findings provide theoretical insight into the maximum entropy method and suggest guidelines for choosing priors and noise levels in analytic continuation.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

We introduce a linear-scaling stochastic method to compute real-space maps of any positive local spectral operator in a tight-binding model. By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral operators in tight-binding models using Markov inequality to bound sampling error.
motivation: To efficiently compute real-space maps of local observables in large tight-binding systems without full diagonalization.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error per site, achieving linear scaling with system size.
result: The method provides rigorous error bounds and linear-scaling computational cost, demonstrated on graphene nanoribbons.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient and reliable computation of local spectral properties in large quantum systems.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, and Ke Lu

As a nontrivial state of solid, Schwarz crystal manifests itself in extremely refined nanograins and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) grain boundaries, and therefore exceptional thermal and mechanical stability. However, it remains unexploited how the structural units interact and thermal tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Schwarz crystals, a nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries, focusing on their structural and thermal properties.
motivation: Schwarz crystals exhibit exceptional thermal and mechanical stability, but the interaction of structural units and thermal transport mechanisms are not well understood.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to investigate the structural confinement and thermal transport in Schwarz crystals.
result: They find that the unique grain boundary structure leads to suppressed thermal conductivity and enhanced stability.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design of nanostructured materials with tailored thermal properties.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala
abstract:
Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the aging behavior of topologically constrained ring polymers is important for polymer physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of dense ring-polymer systems with varying stiffness are performed to monitor dynamical arrest after instantaneous thermal quenches.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with stiffer rings exhibiting slower relaxation and more pronounced aging effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the glass transition in ring polymers but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring physics models using large language models.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific discovery process, but the paper focuses on AI methodology rather than advancing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids is driven by rare cage escapes rather than collective rearrangements.
conclusion: Rare cage escapes are the dominant relaxation mechanism in deeply supercooled liquids, providing new insights into glassy dynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; bridging this gap is necessary to validate quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new computational complexity arguments, including average-case hardness and anticoncentration, tailored to the saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with the number of modes.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime is hard for classical computers under standard complexity assumptions, extending the theoretical basis for quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The results provide rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, confirming that they are indeed hard to simulate classically.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and can be detected via neutron scattering.
motivation: Understanding the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons and analyze their low-energy excitations.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The findings suggest that chiral solitons are detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, but the work is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs on a sphere, using numerical techniques.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute scaling dimensions and operator spectra.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable non-perturbative tool for studying fermionic CFTs and reveals emergent supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré materials is important for potential information manipulation, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for manipulating information via spin textures, but does not directly address quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To predict physical links in networks where direct observation is difficult.
method: Uses a physics-informed approach combining network science and dynamical systems theory.
result: The framework successfully infers causal links across a range of networked dynamics.
conclusion: The method provides a general tool for link prediction in complex networks.
