title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices, which is important for low-dissipation electronics.
method: Local protonic gating is applied to gate-defined homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect while preserving time-reversal symmetry.
result: The authors observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect without an external magnetic field, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diodes in homojunctions, with potential applications in superconducting electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the three-dimensional XY universality class and nonlinear magnetic susceptibility in a kagome ice compound HoAgGe, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements and neutron scattering experiments were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, and the transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic properties of kagome ice compounds and the role of universality in phase transitions.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new material platform for investigating flat-band physics at room temperature, which could enable studies of correlated phenomena without cryogenic constraints.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material with potential for topological phases.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy combined with magneto-optical measurements under varying electric fields.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field-driven transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a platform for studying and controlling quantum anomalous Hall states, with implications for topological electronics.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the resulting complex domain structures.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were applied to Ni₂MnBO₅ to identify and distinguish the different ferroic orders and their domain walls.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to the formation of complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The study reveals a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for multifunctional materials.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in two-dimensional photonic crystals with stealthy hyperuniform disorder, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show unexpected scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale silicon photonic crystals are fabricated and characterized experimentally, with theoretical modeling of radiative loss effects.
result: Residual scattering is observed and attributed to radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of radiative loss in disordered photonic crystals, important for photonic device design.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing and electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control and spin-dependent electron optics in graphene for spintronic applications.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control via spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for spin control in graphene, relevant to spintronics but not to the specified research directions.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than specific technical results.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by outlining a structured path forward.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework with five stages, each defined by key scientific and engineering milestones.
result: A high-level roadmap for quantum computing development is provided, but no novel technical contributions or experimental results are reported.
conclusion: The framework serves as a guide for the field but does not advance any specific direction in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and interactions with light, phonons, and electric fields.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving and opening new directions for applications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic waves.
result: They show that both optical and acoustic forces and torques can be described by similar conservation laws and stress tensors.
conclusion: The unified perspective aids in designing advanced particle manipulation techniques across optics and acoustics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a unified view of dynamical evolution by treating space and time on the same footing.
method: The review focuses on space-time duality in interacting many-body systems and its relationship with brickwork quantum circuits, drawing analogies with digital computation.
result: The paper presents a pedagogical exposition of how space-time duality enables exact solvability of certain quantum many-body dynamics.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful framework for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a platform for realizing novel electronic states driven by frustration and interference.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in complex systems like ecology and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across different fields.
method: Uses field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism) to derive and solve master equations for reaction-diffusion processes.
result: Provides a unified framework for analyzing stochastic dynamics in chemical, ecological, and epidemiological systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a fundamental photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-oriented studies.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on future directions for integrating these models into practical applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are advancing, but further development is needed to fully exploit them in photonics and energy harvesting technologies.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum tunneling, and quantum-classical correspondence.
result: It highlights quantum effects such as skyrmion tunneling and quantum fluctuations, and discusses how these could enable new functionalities.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for novel quantum technologies, but many open questions remain.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, it is crucial to investigate spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and astrophysical observations.
result: The review provides a comprehensive summary of current constraints on spin-dependent interactions and discusses future experimental prospects.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, and further experimental and theoretical work is needed to explore their implications for dark matter and fundamental symmetries.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where bounds are exceeded, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made under conditions that invalidate the assumptions of the bounds, and shows how to design materials that exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplication of the bounds; this insight can guide development of materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in various quantum platforms.
result: Summarizes current capabilities and challenges in engineering synthetic quantum matter in fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional spaces.
conclusion: These nonstandard geometries offer new avenues for quantum simulation but are not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and gravity-induced entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement mediation) and experimental approaches (matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with quantum systems.
result: Current experiments are underway to detect gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement, which will guide the theoretical description of gravity at the laboratory scale.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to explore the interface of quantum mechanics and gravity, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Atomic Clock Frequency Ratios With Fractional Uncertainty $≤3.2×{10}^{−18}$
authors: Alexander Aeppli et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Aeppli et al. (BACON Collaboration)

We report high-precision frequency ratio measurements between optical atomic clocks based on [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. With total fractional uncertainties at or below [MATH], these measurements meet an important milestone criterion for redefinit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033201] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: High-precision frequency ratio measurements between optical atomic clocks with fractional uncertainty below 3.2e-18.
motivation: To meet a milestone criterion for redefinition of the second and to test fundamental physics.
method: Frequency ratio measurements using optical atomic clocks based on different atomic species.
result: Achieved total fractional uncertainties at or below 3.2e-18.
conclusion: These measurements support the redefinition of the second and provide stringent tests of fundamental constants.

title: Hidden Density-Wave Instability In The Trimer Ruthenate ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ru}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10}$
authors: Gang Cao, Hengdi Zhao, Adrienne Bond, Tristan R. Cao, Gabriel Schebel, Arabella Quane, Yifei Ni, Yu Zhang, Logan Wall, Rahul Nandkishore, Pedro Schlottmann, Stephan Rosenkranz, And Feng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Gang Cao, Hengdi Zhao, Adrienne Bond, Tristan R. Cao, Gabriel Schebel, Arabella Quane, Yifei Ni, Yu Zhang, Logan Wall, Rahul Nandkishore, Pedro Schlottmann, Stephan Rosenkranz, and Feng Ye

Simultaneous signatures in structure, thermodynamics, and transport reveal a strongly pinned density-wave in an antiferromagnetic oxide previously regarded as a purely magnetic insulator.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036502] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a hidden density-wave instability in a trimer ruthenate, previously considered a purely magnetic insulator.
motivation: To understand the interplay between structure, thermodynamics, and transport in antiferromagnetic oxides, and to reveal hidden electronic instabilities.
method: Combined structural, thermodynamic, and transport measurements on Ba4Ru3O10 single crystals.
result: Simultaneous signatures in structure, thermodynamics, and transport indicate a strongly pinned density-wave order.
conclusion: The material exhibits a hidden density-wave instability beyond its previously known magnetic properties.

title: Geometric Mechanisms Enabling Spin- And Enantio-sensitive Observables In One-photon Ionization Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Philip Caesar M. Flores, Stefanos Carlström, Serguei Patchkovskii, Misha Ivanov, Andres F. Ordonez, And Olga Smirnova
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies spin-resolved photoionization of chiral molecules, focusing on geometric mechanisms for spin- and enantio-sensitive observables.

result: Identifies geometric mechanisms that give rise to spin- and enantio-sensitive observables in one-photon ionization.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into chiral molecule photoionization dynamics and potential applications in enantio-detection.

title: Pressure-induced Structural Transitions And Dome-shaped Superconductivity In The Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{PbBi}}_{6}{\mathrm{Te}}_{10}$
authors: Junying Hu, Guangyang Dai, Liang Ma, Jingkai Bi, Jianyong Chen, And Zhiwei Men
abstract:
Author(s): JunYing Hu, GuangYang Dai, Liang Ma, JingKai Bi, JianYong Chen, and ZhiWei Men

Topological insulators (TIs) constitute a unique class of quantum materials owing to their topology-protected electron states. While pressure is an effective way to induce superconductivity in TIs, superconductivity often appears after phase transition or structural disorder. Therefore, identifying …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024103] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pressure-induced structural transitions and superconductivity in the topological insulator PbBi6Te10.
motivation: Topological insulators can become superconducting under pressure, but the relationship between structural changes and superconductivity is not well understood.
method: The authors perform high-pressure experiments, including X-ray diffraction and electrical transport measurements, to track structural and superconducting properties.
result: They observe a dome-shaped superconducting phase and identify structural transitions that correlate with the emergence of superconductivity.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the interplay between structural disorder and superconductivity in topological insulators.

title: Ultrafast Nonthermal Suppression Of Ferroelectricity By Carrier Screening In ${\mathrm{LiNbO}}_{3}$
authors: Man Tou Wong, Zhuquan Zhang, Zi-Jie Liu, And Keith A. Nelson
abstract:
Author(s): Man Tou Wong, Zhuquan Zhang, Zi-Jie Liu, and Keith A. Nelson

Ferroelectric materials are key to energy-efficient electronics, memory, and optical applications. While charge carriers typically screen and suppress ferroelectricity, their role under nonequilibrium conditions remains elusive. Here, we use femtosecond laser pulses to liberate trapped carriers in $…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034309] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast suppression of ferroelectricity in LiNbO3 via carrier screening using femtosecond laser pulses.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium carrier screening in ferroelectrics is important for energy-efficient electronics and memory applications.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses are used to liberate trapped carriers, and the resulting suppression of ferroelectricity is probed.
result: The authors observe nonthermal suppression of ferroelectric order due to carrier screening on ultrafast timescales.
conclusion: Carrier screening can dynamically control ferroelectric properties, offering a route for ultrafast switching in ferroelectric devices.

title: Deep Learning Approach For Arpes And Time-resolved Arpes: Gradient Attention U-net For Denoising And Reconstruction
authors: Gongyi Cheng, Ziyang Guo, Zhengcong Yan, Xiaochuan Ma, Yichen Qiu, Guangzhen Shen, Xintong Li, Shijing Tan, And Bing Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Gongyi Cheng, Ziyang Guo, Zhengcong Yan, Xiaochuan Ma, Yichen Qiu, Guangzhen Shen, Xintong Li, Shijing Tan, and Bing Wang

Data analysis in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and time-resolved ARPES usually employs derivative-based methods, such as second derivative and maximum curvature, to enhance spectral visibility. Despite their widespread use, these methods are prone to noise amplification and the i…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055414] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies a deep learning U-net model to denoise and reconstruct ARPES and time-resolved ARPES spectra.
motivation: Traditional derivative-based methods for enhancing ARPES spectra amplify noise and introduce artifacts, motivating a deep learning approach for improved denoising and reconstruction.
method: The authors propose a Gradient Attention U-net (GAU-net) that incorporates gradient information and attention mechanisms to effectively denoise and reconstruct ARPES and tr-ARPES data.
result: The GAU-net outperforms traditional methods and other deep learning baselines in terms of denoising quality and reconstruction accuracy on simulated and experimental data.
conclusion: Deep learning, specifically the proposed GAU-net, provides a powerful tool for processing ARPES data, enabling clearer visualization of electronic band structures.

title: Many-body Interactions In The Dielectric Theory Of Stopping Power Of Solids For Classical And Quantum Projectiles
authors: Vladimir U. Nazarov And Vyacheslav M. Silkin
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir U. Nazarov and Vyacheslav M. Silkin

We take account of the many-body dynamic interactions by including the wave-vector and frequency-dependent exchange-correlation (xc) kernel [MATH] in the framework of the dielectric theory of the stopping power of crystals for moving charges. The cases of classical and qu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014308] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies many-body interactions in the dielectric theory of stopping power of solids for charged projectiles, a topic in condensed matter physics.
motivation: To improve the theoretical description of energy loss of charged particles moving through solids by including exchange-correlation effects.
method: The authors incorporate a wave-vector and frequency-dependent exchange-correlation kernel into the dielectric function formalism.
result: They derive stopping power formulas for both classical and quantum projectiles, accounting for many-body dynamic interactions.
conclusion: The inclusion of exchange-correlation effects leads to more accurate predictions of stopping power in solids.

title: Microscopic Origin Of Polarization-controlled Magnetization Switching In ${\mathrm{FePt}/\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$
authors: Qurat Ul Ain, Thi H. Ho, Soon Cheol Hong, Dorj Odkhuu, And S. H. Rhim
abstract:
Author(s): Qurat ul ain, Thi H. Ho, Soon Cheol Hong, Dorj Odkhuu, and S. H. Rhim

Electric-field driven magnetization switching in [MATH] (001) is demonstrated through first-principles calculations. The magnetic easy axis of the FePt layer undergoes a transition from an in-plane to perpendicular direction upon ferroelectric polarization switching, a …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024414] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field-driven magnetization switching in FePt/BaTiO3 using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of polarization-controlled magnetization switching in multiferroic heterostructures.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations are performed on FePt/BaTiO3 (001) to compute magnetic anisotropy and electronic structure.
result: The magnetic easy axis of FePt switches from in-plane to perpendicular upon ferroelectric polarization reversal of BaTiO3.
conclusion: The study reveals a microscopic origin for magnetoelectric coupling in this system, which could be useful for spintronic devices.

title: Designing Multiple Multiferroic Orders In Altermagnetic Transition Metal Oxytrihalides
authors: Chao Yang, Tao Li, Chenqiang Hua, Yao Wang, Yin Wang, And Tai Min
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Yang, Tao Li, Chenqiang Hua, Yao Wang, Yin Wang, and Tai Min

Multiferroic altermagnets, which integrate ferroelectricity with altermagnetism, provide a promising platform for realizing unconventional magnetoelectric coupling. However, the realization of multiple multiferroic orders in such systems remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover electrically reco…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055411] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts multiple multiferroic orders in altermagnetic transition metal oxytrihalides using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Multiferroic altermagnets are promising for unconventional magnetoelectric coupling, but multiple multiferroic orders in such systems remain unexplored.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory are used to study the electronic structure and ferroelectric polarization of the materials.
result: Electrically reversible ferroelectric polarization and multiple multiferroic orders are predicted in the altermagnetic oxytrihalides.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to realize multiple multiferroic orders in altermagnetic systems, potentially enabling new magnetoelectric devices.

title: Quantum Disorder Engineering In Superconducting Ti(O,N) Thin Films
authors: Fengmiao Li, Solveig Aamlid, Oliver A. Dicks, Myung-Geun Han, Giorgio Levy, Ronny Sutarto, Zhihao Chen, Chong Liu, Hsiang-Hsi Kung, Simon Godin, Bruce A. Davidson, Zhi Gang Cheng, Andrea Damascelli, Yimei Zhu, Christoph Heil, Ilya Elfimov, George A. Sawatzky, And Ke Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Fengmiao Li, Solveig Aamlid, Oliver A. Dicks, Myung-Geun Han, Giorgio Levy, Ronny Sutarto, Zhihao Chen, Chong Liu, Hsiang-Hsi Kung, Simon Godin, Bruce A. Davidson, Zhi Gang Cheng, Andrea Damascelli, Yimei Zhu, Christoph Heil, Ilya Elfimov, George A. Sawatzky, and Ke Zou

Nitrogen substitution for oxygen is an anion-engineering strategy for tailoring the rich physical properties of oxides. In this work, we investigate the effect of nitrogen doping in titanium monoxide (TiO) and the underlying mechanism, utilizing epitaxial titanium oxynitride Ti(O,N) films grown usin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065415] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nitrogen doping in titanium monoxide thin films to engineer disorder and tune physical properties.
motivation: To understand how anion substitution (N for O) affects the electronic and structural properties of TiO, enabling tailored functionalities.
method: Epitaxial Ti(O,N) thin films were grown and characterized using X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and transport measurements, combined with theoretical calculations.
result: Nitrogen doping introduces disorder and modifies the electronic structure, leading to changes in conductivity and optical properties.
conclusion: Anion engineering via nitrogen substitution is an effective strategy to control disorder and properties in titanium oxynitride films.

title: Polarization Conversion In Time-modulated Magnetized Plasmas: Faraday Configuration
authors: Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, And Mark A. Cappelli
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, and Mark A. Cappelli

In this paper, we address the problem of wave propagation within an unbounded time-modulated magnetized plasma in a Faraday configuration. We present an analysis formulated by coupling Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic evolution equation for the plasma current density, and casting the result…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave propagation in time-modulated magnetized plasmas, focusing on polarization conversion in the Faraday configuration.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in time-varying plasmas is important for applications in plasma physics and electromagnetic wave control.
method: The authors couple Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic plasma current density equation and analyze the resulting system for the Faraday configuration.
result: The analysis yields conditions for polarization conversion and wave propagation characteristics in the time-modulated plasma.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into wave behavior in dynamic plasma media, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mechanical Waveform Memory In An Athermal Random Medium
authors: Eamon Dwight And D. Candela
abstract:
Author(s): Eamon Dwight and D. Candela

This manuscript investigates static waveform memory in a system of jammed, soft, frictional particles. It is shown that a small, time-dependent shear strain applied during progressive compression can imprint an arbitrary waveform, which is recalled in time-reversed order upon decompression. The conditions that allow memory formation and the limits of memory readout are established.

#TimelyTopic #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mechanical waveform memory in a jammed granular system, demonstrating that shear strain during compression can imprint and recall waveforms.
motivation: Understanding memory formation in disordered athermal systems is of fundamental interest in soft matter physics.
method: The authors apply a time-dependent shear strain during progressive compression of jammed frictional particles and measure the recalled waveform upon decompression.
result: They show that arbitrary waveforms can be imprinted and recalled in time-reversed order, and characterize the conditions and limits of this memory effect.
conclusion: The work reveals a novel form of memory in athermal granular media, but it is not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Random Motility Regulation As A Generic Mechanism Of Community Formation
authors: Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, and Julien Tailleur

The self-organization of microbial ecosystems involves a large variety of mechanisms, ranging from biochemical signaling to population dynamics. Among these, the role of motility regulation has been little studied, despite the importance of active migration processes. Here we show how weak, random m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random motility regulation in microbial communities leads to self-organization, using a theoretical model of active particles.
motivation: Understanding the role of motility regulation in microbial ecosystem self-organization, which is little studied compared to biochemical signaling and population dynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model where particles undergo random motility changes and analyze the resulting collective behavior using statistical physics and active matter theory.
result: Weak, random motility regulation can drive community formation and spatial structure in microbial populations.
conclusion: Random motility regulation is a generic mechanism for community formation in microbial ecosystems, with implications for understanding natural and engineered microbial systems.

title: Short Peptide-grafted Interfaces Regulate Protein Cluster Coacervation
authors: Chen-Yang Fan, Chun-Lai Ren, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Chen-yang Fan, Chun-lai Ren, and Yu-qiang Ma

The behavior of protein condensates driven by weak multivalent interactions has been extensively studied in bulk systems, yet their interfacial behavior remains far less explored. Using coarse-grained simulations, we investigated protein clusters adsorbed onto interfaces grafted with short peptides …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies protein cluster coacervation at peptide-grafted interfaces using coarse-grained simulations.
motivation: Understanding interfacial behavior of protein condensates is important for biological and materials applications, but remains poorly understood compared to bulk systems.
method: Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations are used to model protein clusters adsorbed onto interfaces grafted with short peptides.
result: The study reveals how grafted peptides regulate the coacervation and morphology of protein clusters at interfaces.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into designing interfaces that control protein condensation, relevant to biomaterials and cellular organization.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in van der Waals heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling the microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time-resolved spectroscopy and theoretical modeling to investigate how excitation energy influences the charge transfer dynamics.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways that depend on the excitation energy, revealing a mechanism for tuning charge transfer efficiency.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for optimizing van der Waals heterostructures for optoelectronic applications.

We develop an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the saddle-point equations (SPEs) governing direct above-threshold ionization (ATI) within the strong-field approximation. This setting provides a well-understood test bed in which the saddle-point structure is known for tail…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033029] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations for above-threshold ionization in strong-field physics.
motivation: Saddle-point equations in strong-field physics are computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that is efficient and accurate.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations without labeled data, incorporating the physical equations as constraints.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point solutions for direct above-threshold ionization, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a promising alternative for solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, potentially extending to more complex scenarios.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for designing nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how an external electric field modulates interlayer interactions and sliding resistance in h-BN.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly alter the interlayer binding energy and friction forces, enabling tunable sliding resistance.
conclusion: External electric fields provide a viable route to control friction in layered materials like h-BN, with potential applications in nanoscale lubrication and mechanical systems.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and dynamical systems.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding anisotropy in silica films can inform better coating design.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films, including anisotropy and its response to heat treatment.
result: They discover hidden anisotropy in silica films that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating performance.
conclusion: The findings guide strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal unique critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to condensed matter physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave events and X-ray pulse profiles, compared to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized.
conclusion: Future observations will further constrain the equation of state, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the review aims to showcase how three real-space techniques can be combined to characterize defects.
method: The paper reviews scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined applications for compound semiconductors.
result: The review demonstrates that combining these techniques provides a more complete picture of atomic-scale disorder and defects.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods, especially when used together, are powerful tools for understanding disorder in semiconductors.

title: Detecting Solenoidal Plasma Turbulence Via Laser Polarization Rotation
authors: Kenan Qu And Nathaniel J. Fisch
abstract:
Author(s): Kenan Qu and Nathaniel J. Fisch

Recent theoretical studies suggest that solenoidal turbulence can significantly enhance fusion reactivity, yet no standard diagnostic exists to directly measure these solenoidal flows in high-energy-density plasmas, nor to distinguish between solenoidal and compressional turbulence. We propose a met…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 035101] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a laser-based diagnostic to detect solenoidal plasma turbulence in fusion reactors.
motivation: Solenoidal turbulence may enhance fusion reactivity, but no direct diagnostic exists to measure it in high-energy-density plasmas.
method: The authors propose using laser polarization rotation as a metrological technique to distinguish solenoidal from compressional turbulence.
result: The method provides a way to directly measure solenoidal flows, which could help validate theoretical predictions.
conclusion: This diagnostic could be important for fusion research but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference Via Reuse For Gravitational-Wave Analyses
authors: Michael J. Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Michael J. Williams

We introduce accelerated sequential posterior inference via reuse (ASPIRE), a broadly applicable framework that transforms existing posterior samples and Bayesian evidence estimates into unbiased results under alternative models without rerunning the original analysis. ASPIRE combines normalizing fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021410] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for accelerating sequential posterior inference in gravitational-wave analyses using normalizing flows.
motivation: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation is computationally expensive, and re-running analyses for alternative models is inefficient.
method: ASPIRE transforms existing posterior samples and Bayesian evidence estimates into unbiased results under alternative models without rerunning the original analysis, using normalizing flows.
result: The method achieves significant computational speedups while maintaining unbiasedness.
conclusion: ASPIRE provides a broadly applicable framework for efficient Bayesian inference in gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: Cavendish Tests Of Millicharged Particles
authors: Asher Berlin, Zachary Bogorad, Peter W. Graham, And Harikrishnan Ramani
abstract:
Author(s): Asher Berlin, Zachary Bogorad, Peter W. Graham, and Harikrishnan Ramani

Decades-old experiments have now been enlisted to set new bounds on the properties of a hypothetical particle that bears a tiny fraction of the electron’s charge.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021804] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses historical Cavendish-type experiments to set new bounds on millicharged particles.
motivation: Millicharged particles are hypothetical particles with a tiny fraction of the electron's charge, and their existence is constrained by various experiments. The authors aim to leverage old Cavendish experiments to improve these constraints.
method: The authors reinterpret data from classic Cavendish torsion balance experiments, which test the inverse-square law of electrostatics, to derive limits on the charge of millicharged particles.
result: New upper bounds on the charge of millicharged particles are obtained, improving upon previous constraints for certain mass ranges.
conclusion: Old Cavendish experiments remain useful for probing new physics, providing competitive constraints on millicharged particles.

title: Positron Annihilation In Multiprincipal Element Alloys For The Identification Of Chemical Short-Range-Order Structures
authors: Qigui Yang, Qianqian Wang, Yao Yu, Te Zhu, Peng Zhang, Ping Wang, Yiping Lu, And Xingzhong Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Qigui Yang, Qianqian Wang, Yao Yu, Te Zhu, Peng Zhang, Ping Wang, Yiping Lu, and Xingzhong Cao

Chemical short-range order (SRO) is an intrinsic feature of the atomic structures in multiprincipal element alloys (MPEAs). Effective control of SRO structures could considerably improve the strength and ductility of MPEAs. However, the experimental characterization of SRO remains highly challenging…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026101] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses positron annihilation spectroscopy to characterize chemical short-range order in multiprincipal element alloys.
motivation: Chemical short-range order (SRO) is crucial for the mechanical properties of multiprincipal element alloys, but experimental characterization is challenging.
method: Positron annihilation spectroscopy is employed to probe atomic-scale defects and local chemical environments in the alloys.
result: The technique successfully identifies SRO structures, providing a new experimental method for SRO characterization.
conclusion: Positron annihilation spectroscopy is an effective tool for studying SRO in multiprincipal element alloys, which can aid in material design.

result: The study provides a framework for extracting molecular asymmetry from HHG spectra on a subcycle timescale.

result: Pb-Pb interactions do not propagate strongly through graphene, and the potential energy surface for Pb adatoms does not inherit the periodicity of the intercalated Pb layer.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and study molecular electronic and vibronic properties at the atomic scale.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling fluorescence imaging of individual molecules and submolecular structures.

abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.

authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.

tldr: This paper reviews low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, covering biological, smart materials, and robotics applications.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment of active units with their velocity leads to novel collective behaviors.
method: Unified mathematical and conceptual framework, review of existing models.
result: Identifies a spectrum of behaviors from single-particle orbits to synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with potential for groundbreaking applications.
